docs.text: Devil Reef Getting In Entering an exposed tidal tunnel, the investigators find passages leading down into the rock. At first they can wade through the thigh-high water in the passages, though a couple of slips show that the way is treacherous. In one chamber, they find old bootlegging gear, at least fifty years old and smelling strongly of brine. They also find a large anemone attached to the ceiling, which drops down to attack but is quickly killed. The noise alerts a group of eight deep ones, who emerge from other tunnels and attack. By confining them to choke points and making good use of their weapons, the team finish these ones off with little fuss. In the next chamber, they see pools of water in the floor, and they can see an underwater tunnel leading from one. Dan Pacho decides to risk it, and swims through the tunnel, emerging in a small chamber with a cracked altar. Upon the alter, he spots a gold cloak - and without hesitation he puts it on, and later is pleased to find out he can swim with great ease. Creeping round the corner, he spots a large crowd of deep ones (at least twenty plus another three of the large hunting deep ones) chanting "Y'ha Nthlei" over and over towards a stone statue wearing a gold crown. He decides to go back and warn the others. The investigators sneak into the chamber and cause a distraction by throwing a petrol bomb at the deep ones. McG lets rip with his flamethrower and Keith shoots Azure Flame everywhere. Dan attacks with his sword, and Peter uses his new machine gun to great effect. Dan does injure his leg though, and decides to disengage from the monsters to pick up the crown and wear it. Eventually all the deep ones are defeated, and Dan narrowly misses becoming cursed. McG notices that the tide appears to be rising unnaturally fast, and he suggests making a break for it back the way they came while they still can. In the chamber with the bootlegging gear, they are dismayed to see the next tunnel completely underwater. Two of the team manage to quickly fashion barrels to provide some advantage when swimming, and they emerge out into the cave leading out - to see the exit being blocked by another hunting deep one. Though everyone is suffering from injuries, they manage to defeat the final enemy - Dan is interested to see that he appears to be extra strong and quick when he is in water and wearing the crown. They swim out to find their boat still there and Old Tom and Amos looking very worried. At that moment however, they hear an enormous rushing sound and see the city from their dreams emerge from the sea. The green spires stretch up into the sky, but then a fog appears that covers everything. After a few seconds the fog is blown away, and the city is gone. Arriving back in Kingsport, the team drive back to Arkham - but when they arrive back, things have changed considerably. Arkham now has alien green spires rising from buildings, there are rivers of fog appearing and disappearing flowing through the streets, and the city appears to be deserted.

docs.text: Horror in High Gear Escape from Innsmouth With the truck loaded up, Amos takes the wheel with McG riding shotgun. Dan, Keith and Peter are in the bed of the truck keeping guard and ready to fend off attacks - which is lucky, as when they pull out of the Marsh Refinery into River Street they are immediately pursued by two motorbikes with riders on the back firing Tommy Guns at them. They shoot one one bike to pieces, which crashes into a building as they make their escape, but after killing the shooter on the second bike Dan decides that he should jump onto the bike himself. With some excellent timing and a lot of luck, he succeeds. McG decides to "help" by shooting the driver of the bike and killing him, but Dan manages to shove the body off and take control of the bike. Two cars attempt to intercept, one chasing from behind and one attempting to ram the truck from the side. Amos manages to manoeuvre the truck skillfully to avoid crashing and McG showers the car with bullets as Keith sets fire to everything around with his Azure Flame. Both cars are eventually put out of action. Three more motorbikes try to intercept, and Peter attempts to duplicate Dan's feat, but does not manage - he is kicked back by the shooter of a bike, and is at risk of falling to the ground, but manages to grab hold of the truck at the last moment, desperately clinging to the side. The team do manage to kill the remaining bikers, with Dan running over the foot of one of them. They are almost out of town when the engine of the truck sputters and dies. McG gets out and is working on the engine when they see a crowd of several hundred people heading towards them with pitchforks and torches. He manages to fix the engine quickly and Amos hastily drives away. As they are leaving Amos, Keith and Peter catch a glimpse of something huge behind them rising from the water and blocking out the stars. They can hear a series of massive crashes behind them, but they turn the corner into the woods and Innsmouth is left behind. When they get to the location where they stashed their car, they load a couple of motorbikes into the bed of the truck and bring all the vehicles back to Arkham. The Terror of Devil Reef At the Clover Club they bring the contraband goods and treasure to Seamus, who is pleased with the results of the excursion. Keith lets slip that there was some monstrosity back at Innsmouth, and Seamus tasks the investigators with the job of ensuring that nothing can be tied back to the O'Bannions and preferably putting a stop to whatever it is. He also tells them that it was reported on the radio that some kind of "natural disaster" has destroyed a large part of Innsmouth overnight. The team fence the treasure that they stole from the refinery and purchase some new guns and armour. The investigators drive to Kingsport and hire Old Tom to take them round the headland and up to Devil Reef off the coast of Innsmouth (since they would definitely run into trouble of several kinds if they went back to Innsmouth directly). The journey takes a couple of hours in the fog, but as they approach Devil Reef the boat is suddenly attacked, with several tentacles grabbing the vessel and an enormous octopus head emerging from the water - though Amos knows this is much smaller than whatever they saw in the distance the previous night. Peter manages to get a critical shot at its head, and fire seems to deal extra damage to it - Amos throws a petrol bomb which causes it a lot of damage, and Keith's Azure Flame comes into play again. Dan manages to chop two tentacles off that were grabbing the boat and before too long the beast is knocked unconscious and then finished off. Keith ponders whether to make calamari. As they approach Devil Reef the investigators notice several tunnels uncovered at low tide. They decide to explore.

docs.text: Reflections in the Depths Escaping the Tower Out of the windows, the investigators see Arkham changed in strange and disturbing ways, with the changes flowing over the city and then disappearing. Another version of Amos suddenly appears in the doorway, saying "Oh my god, you are still alive! You must get out!" before promptly disappearing. McG and Amos lead the way out of the tower to try to find a way down, but when the others turn the corner the two of them have disappeared! Keith leads the way, with Dan, Peter and Father Mateo following. After a few minutes, they bump into future versions of themselves - after an initial bit of confusion they work out what is going on, and future Dan hands present Dan a strange metal rod, which he says might be helpful. After trying to go down and finding themselves back up high, the remaining investigators find past versions of themselves. Present Dan hands past Dan the strange metal rod, which he says might be helpful. Keith has the brainwave that maybe they need to go up to get down to ground level, and sure enough after a few minutes of going to opposite way to what seems necessary, they find themselves out at street level. As they walk through the streets, they see things from various times, some of which appear to be in the future - but some a long way in the past. At one intersection they are approached by three growling wolves, but Peter blasts them with his gun and the third is finished off pretty quickly. The Kelp Club Trying to decide what to do, the investigators head to a nearby club which is playing strange music the like of which they have not heard before. Inside it is deserted, but the bar is lit with strange multicoloured lights and seems to openly stock strange alcoholic drinks from another time. Dan is very keen to try them all, and especially likes the clear spirit with flakes of gold leaf floating in it - he decides to take this bottle and then hunts around in the back room for unopened bottles as well. The others load up a cart with all they can (including wine from 1982 which is very confusing) and they head to the Clover Club to stash it away. At the Clover Club, they enter the back room only to find alternate versions of themselves - Peter Gill is partly transformed into a Deep One, Keith has embraced the power of Ithaqua with glowing blue eyes, Dan's crown is glowing and the cloak has melded with his skin, and Father Mateo is a demonic creature with red skin and smoke rising from his body. At first the fight is pretty even, with both sides inflicting damage on the other - the tide turns when Keith casts Blinding Light which prevents the doppelgangers from dodging and enabling Peter and Dan to inflict massive damage on them. Having finished them all off and stashed the booze, Father Mateo suggests returning to the sanctity of the church to hopefully gain some safety and make sure the other survivors are still okay. Back at the Church Traveling to the church, the team see their past played out in front of them, but not the same way that they remember - they see the car chase, first with them escaping, but then with them on motorbikes chasing down others in the car. They see themselves performing The King in Yellow on Stage in front of an audience of cheering corpses. They see themselves in Hyperborea ruling over the city that has been born again. At the church, they enter and find at least four other versions of themselves (along with versions of McG and Amos) - each with a different story to tell. In some timelines, someone had used the power of the cloak and crown to release Cthulhu. In others, Adelei had merged with Ithaqua, and in others many had succumbed to transforming into deep ones and the remaining humans were in hiding or on the run. In one, someone had sacrificed themselves with the aid of the cloak and the crown to reseal Cthulhu. Another Keith offered present-day Keith the option to merge to gain knowledge that may be helpful, but at the cost of their sanity. Keith accepted, and learnt how to summon a spirit familiar. Dan and Peter also decided to undergo the ritual - each of whom gained skills at the cost of knowing more than they were meant to know. Keith had a vision of Adelei at the Miskatonic Observatory, body wreathed in lightning and blood, completing some sort of ritual - but no clue whether it was to bind or release Cthulhu. The investigators decide to go there to find out!

docs.text: Shadows Over Innsmouth Arrival in Innsmouth Dan arrives at Amos's house early in the morning and wakes everyone up. Keith makes breakfast while McG and Amos examine the engraved sword that they recovered from the seabed. The runes do indeed look Hyperborean, and in Amos's notes he finds reference to something similar in Innsmouth, though without any details. They take a car to the coastal town, which is only about an hour's drive away - though it is known to be unfriendly to strangers. Driving through town, they notice the Marsh Refinery spewing smoke, and park near the Congregational Church. Walking around the area, they notice that they appear to be being followed. The Order of Dagon Hall is by far the nicest building in town, which is otherwise very run down and dilapidated. As they go towards it, they are approached by an old man who warns them cryptically: “The sea remembers. You shouldn’t be here.” The front room of the hall has plenty of people coming in and out and using the meeting rooms there, and examination of the pictures on the wall leads to some clues about the Marsh family. There is a guarded entrance to the back which piques the investigators interest - McG causes a brief distraction and Keith then casts Azure Flame to set fire to a corner of the room. With everyone distracted, they slip through the guarded door. In the back room, they find themselves amongst cases of artifacts, shelves of old books and tomes and a strange altar. Dan secures a way out by breaking the window latch and opening it up. He also manages to lever open one of the cases, stealing a gold necklace set with black pearls. McG picks open another case to take a similar gold crown, and then helps Amos and Keith to snatch as many books as possible. They then climb out the window and hide in an alley while McG retrieves the car and brings it round - everyone piles in and they head speedily back to Arkham to see what they managed to grab. At Amos's house again, they examine the books. Keith is delighted to find the Tome of Oceiros, which has some spells in it. They also find records of the Order of Dagon, which details the deal made with the Deep Ones, where they bred with one of the Marsh family in the past, and their descendants are cursed to turn into Deep Ones as they get older. Part of the town that rebelled 70 years ago was wiped out, and now everyone there is under their influence. The Deep Ones supply gold for the town, which is processed at the Marsh Refinery. There is also details of a sunken city out at Devil Reef, and an altar on the coast near Innsmouth that is visible when the tide is low. McG goes shopping and cobbles together a flame-thrower from the pieces he holds. The Marsh Refinery Heading back at night, the team park near the abandoned railway, and try to sneak into town. At first they are successful, with nobody noticing them as they mirror the unusual shambling gait of the locals. However, just as they approach the refinery, someone shouts a warning. McG quickly picks the lock of the front gate, and they all rush in. Shutting the gate, they find enough empty crates to barricade it and Amos also jams the gate with a metal pole. Dan and Amos hang back to keep watch, while McG finds some fireproof overalls. He starts putting them on, as Peter opens the door into the employee rest area - four men with protruding eyes are already standing with improvised weapons ready to throw, but Peter manages to take two of them out with his shotgun right away. Keith casts Kiss of Brine to knock another one over, and between them they finish the last guy off. In a storeroom on the other side of the refinery, they find crates of contraband - some belonging to the O'Bannions and some from elsewhere. They also find two smaller crates, which they open to find gold coins and black pearls. They discuss how to fence the goods, but at that moment another huge Hunting Deep One and six smaller Deep Ones enter the refinery from the rear. Dan Pacho rushes towards them, and McG tries out his flamethrower to huge success. The Hunting Deep One fails to curse Dan, and falls soon afterwards. The other Deep Ones swipe at Dan, but are taken out without too much bother. The investigators find a truck out the rear entrance, which they load up with the crates as quickly as possible, and decide to head back to Arkham before the whole town comes after them. But will they be pursued?

They then climb out the window and hide in an alley while McG retrieves the car and brings it round - everyone piles in and they head speedily back to Arkham to see what they managed to grab. At Amos's house again, they examine the books. Keith is delighted to find the Tome of Oceiros, which has some spells in it. Part of the town that rebelled 70 years ago was wiped out, and now everyone there is under their influence. The Deep Ones supply gold for the town, which is processed at the Marsh Refinery. There is also details of a sunken city out at Devil Reef, and an altar on the coast near Innsmouth that is visible when the tide is low. McG goes shopping and cobbles together a flame-thrower from the pieces he holds.
docs.title: Arrival in Innsmouth

docs.text: Heading back at night, the team park near the abandoned railway, and try to sneak into town. At first they are successful, with nobody noticing them as they mirror the unusual shambling gait of the locals. However, just as they approach the refinery, someone shouts a warning. McG quickly picks the lock of the front gate, and they all rush in. Shutting the gate, they find enough empty crates to barricade it and Amos also jams the gate with a metal pole. Dan and Amos hang back to keep watch, while McG finds some fireproof overalls. He starts putting them on, as Peter opens the door into the employee rest area - four men with protruding eyes are already standing with improvised weapons ready to throw, but Peter manages to take two of them out with his shotgun right away. Keith casts Kiss of Brine to knock another one over, and between them they finish the last guy off. In a storeroom on the other side of the refinery, they find crates of contraband - some belonging to the O'Bannions and some from elsewhere. They also find two smaller crates, which they open to find gold coins and black pearls. They discuss how to fence the goods, but at that moment another huge Hunting Deep One and six smaller Deep Ones enter the refinery from the rear. Dan Pacho rushes towards them, and McG tries out his flamethrower to huge success. The Hunting Deep One fails to curse Dan, and falls soon afterwards. The other Deep Ones swipe at Dan, but are taken out without too much bother. The investigators find a truck out the rear entrance, which they load up with the crates as quickly as possible, and decide to head back to Arkham before the whole town comes after them. But will they be pursued?
docs.title: The Marsh Refinery

docs.text: The Abyss Stares Back The Descent Below After the attack by the Deep Ones, the team decide to back to Kingsport briefly to hire some additional diving equipment. McG drives the boat around in circles before Peter takes the helm. They leave the cargo ship and Eli at the docks, warning him to stay quiet for now. Back at the location they found using the map, Dan and Peter put the diving suits on and go over the side to have a look around. They see bodies of dead sailors floating in the water, with an unsettling jerk every once in a while. There is an eerie glow coming from some of the stones of an old ruin here, and they also see some crates scattered around. Looking in some of the crates, they find bottles of whiskey and guns, and they start the process to load them onto the boat. Dan also finds a box made of a mysterious substance, and inside a sword engraved with runes. At that moment, a huge hunting deep one attacks them underwater, and at the same moment four smaller deep ones climb up the side of the boat to attack McG and Keith. Dan uses the sword, and as it cuts into the hunting deep one, the runes glow briefly. He does a lot of damage, and then Peter finishes it off with a harpoon throw to the head. McG and Keith manage to finish off the deep ones on the boat. All in all, the team recover Three crates of high-end whiskey Two crates of luxury canned goods including caviar One crate of rifles as well as the sword. Dan takes a look at the glowing stonework, and thinks it is similar to what he saw in Hyperborea - but all he can see is a fallen over doorway half buried in the silt. Return to Kingsport The investigators patch themselves up as they head back to Kingsport. The O'Bannion workers hired to collect the goods from the boat unload what there is and drive off in a hurry, saying that they were disturbed to see a couple of people just walking off the docks and into the sea. On the way back to Arkham, Dan drinks a lot of whiskey to try to settle his nerves - he does a little, but he also ends up drunk. The Dreaming Ones At the Clover Club, Seamus is angry that only some of the goods have been recovered, but as McG is giving his report, a waitress suddenly stiffens, her eyes rolling back, and she starts speaking in a deep, rumbling voice — not her own. Then, the walls tremble, and twisted figures of shadow emerge from the corners of the room, clawing toward the investigators. McG tries to subdue the waitress, seeing that she is scared and that maybe something is possessing her. Failing to do that, he then shoots her. The others attack the shadows, but find that their guns do little damage. As the shadows tough the investigators, they are temporarily dragged into a dream-state. Keith's casting of Azure Flame and Dan's sword make short work of them however, until the enchantment on the sword backfires and hurts Dan. They finish the last shadow - as each of them is destroyed, the investigator fighting them hears a voice in their head say "The Sleeper will know your names." Seamus appears to no longer trust the investigators and orders them to fix this mess before storming out. The investigators rest and decide to meet at Amos's house in the morning to decide on their next move. That night they sleep restlessly, and in their dreams they see the green city again — only this time, something is awake within it.

docs.text: The Merging of Worlds Searching for Survivors The investigators have to leave their car as they come to Arkham, as the streets are blocked with vehicles that look like they have been abandoned mid-drive. They make their way to Amos's house - as they pass other houses, they see meals left half-eaten on the tables, books dropped on the floor, all signs that whatever made the people disappear, it was sudden. At Amos's house, they enter and find writing on the wall. McG and Amos manage to decipher some of it, which appears to warn about the fog. At this time, they notice a large bank of fog moving towards the house - and out of the fog they hear the sound of wet footsteps. A group of mindless thralls with bulging eyes and gill-like slits on their throats attack the investigators. The team manage to dispose of them, though at one point McG runs away screaming. As the fog moves on, they see other thralls mindlessly following in its wake. They decide to follow, and as they approach French Hill, they see a face emerge from a church and beckon them in. Father Mateo introduces himself along with a couple of dozen other survivors. They tell of when the fog rolled in, and suddenly the city was not itself anymore. Strange shapes moved through the streets, and anyone who heard their whispers vanished. A few people resisted the change, but most walked willingly toward the spires, vanishing inside. They saw figures in robes, performing some kind of ritual at the Miskatonic Museum. The investigators decide to see whether there is anything still there. At the Museum Father Mateo comes with them, and they enter the museum without any trouble. It's dark inside - the main lights are not working, but the display lights are providing illumination. As the team split up to investigate, the huge formless blob of a shoggoth drops from the ceiling and starts slithering towards them, eyes and tentacles appearing and disappearing on its outer membrane. It knocks over Peter and Dan, who desperately fight back against it. McG uses a petrol bomb against it, and breaks his flamethrower attacking it - it is vulnerable to fire, so this does help. Eventually the shoggoth is defeated, and the team can take a look around the museum. Most things look normal, but one particular display looks like it has had a strange wooden idol stolen from it. The description of the idol tells them that it was discovered underwater near Devil Reef, and that it had some strange script on the base. Amos and Keith recognise the symbols as being similar to one particular alien spire that they passed on the way here. The Green Spires The team find the spire with the symbols on, and start to make their way up. The passages in the tower seem to deft logic, with windows showing different heights and different angles of the city. Eventually they climb to the top of a spiral staircase and find themselves in a forest clearing with puddles around them. A Deep One Cultist is performing a ritual at an altar, and four Hunting Deep Ones protect it. As the investigators attack, they find that their shots on the cultist are deflected to the hunters. Nevertheless, they manage to take down all the deep ones and stop the ritual. They find themselves back in the top in a room at the top - looking out over Arkham, they see the city flicker between the normal version, the version with the underwater city and then a few other versions seem to overlap as well!

docs.text: Cultists Among Us The Police Station At the police station, Rita sneaks up near a couple of officers and overhears that Billy Cooper is at the graveyard. Taking Joe's car, the investigators drive there and through the fog they see a group of 5 ghouls digging away at some graves. Near them, Billy is leaning against a gravestone taking notes in a small book. Rita sneaks up near Billy, and at that moment two things happen: Joe shoots a shotgun at Billy Cooper, catching him in one arm and disabling it, and William Yorick throws a Molotov Cocktail at the ghouls, setting them all on fire. With half the ghouls falling down from this attack, Daisy helps to finish them off with some more casts of Shriveling. Rita goes on the offensive with her new baseball bat. She picks up a minor wound as Billy shoots back, but otherwise escapes with no injury as Billy is knocked to the ground, disabled. Reading the notebook, the investigators find out the ghouls' weaknesses . St. Mary's Hospital Heading to the hospital, Loretta Clark is on duty. Having said that they come at the request of Carolyn Fern, Loretta asks them to investigate one of the corridors that she has heard disturbances in. Rita picks up a first-aid kit and notices deep claw marks gouged into the floor and a blood-stained shirt sleeve. Loretta is convinced to give up her key for the team to investigate further. They go downstairs and meet the guard on his patrol, but as he introduces himself a ghoul bursts out of a nearby room and rips his throat out, while another drops from a vent in the ceiling. The investigators then finish these ghouls off, but another two ghouls and an especially large and fierce ghoul them burst out from the morgue and attack. Rita takes a large number of wounds, but in the meantime the large ghoul is severely injured and incapacitated by the other investigators. Rita manages to patch herself up with the first-aid kit, and the team finish off the remaining ghouls. Investigating the morgue and Ruth Turner's desk, they find some notes she made describing how trepidatious she was feeling at the prospect of becoming a ghoul, and describes the site of the ritual in the woods. Ambush from the Skies Rita has had enough and takes a break to head back home and rest up. Heading to the river docs to meet Joey "The Rat" Virgil, the rest of the investigators are shocked when the dead body of a man suddenly falls from the sky and smashes into a car in front of them. Two nightgaunts start to close in. Joe shoots one with his shotgun, and Daisy manages to case Shriveling on the other before one casts a spell that envelops everyone in thick smoke. One of the nightgaunts snatches William and carries him up into the skiy, but William manages to whack it with his spade - but at the expense of his leg which cracks when he is dropped to the ground. Meanwhile, Daisy goes in for an attack up close, but is also damaged in the leg when the nightgaunt stabs it with its tail. Eventually, the nightgaunts are defeated, and Joe pools everyone's money together to purchase a Tommy Gun from Joey, which he equips (passing the shotgun on to William to use). A quick side-trip to Ye Olde Magick Shoppe means that Daisy also pick up an Elder Sign talisman. The Professor's House Peter Warren's house is empty when the investigators get there. They discuss how best to break the door down when Lita Chantler turns up again and confidently picks the lock. Joe makes himself at home and starts making a sandwich in the kitchen, while William retreats to the toilet again. After looking around for a while, the investigators hear footsteps coming up the path and ready themselves. Peter Warren enters the house with a couple of cultists and seems confident in overcoming any opposition. He seems likely to succeed when William shoots into the ceiling and he dodges Joe's bullets, however he falls to Daisy's shriveling spell and Lita shooting him with her pistol. Once he is out of the picture, the cultists fall soon after, and the team find a note with details of the ritual .

docs.text: The Howl of the Hounds Let's Get Our Story Straight The investigators meet up at Joe Diamond's house to talk about what they know and figure out where their first lead is. Rita Young and Daisy Walker translate a strange coded message that refers to an "eternal one" and is signed by Peter Warren . Daisy knows where he lives. Rita laments the lack of coffee at Joe's house. William Yorick finds a common theme in the inaccurate documentation from the morgue at St. Mary's Hospital, as they are signed by Ruth Turner . He also hides in various bathrooms, perhaps because he is nervous? Joe Diamond suspects there is a cover-up by the police, and a stack of disappearance reports are signed by Billy Cooper . He also receives a phone call from Carolyn Fern, who is concerned that her friend Loretta Clark has been feeling anxious working the graveyard shift at the hospital. We're Not Alone A crash comes from the cellar. The investigators move into the kitchen, and see that there is a strange mist behind the windows, blocking the view from outside. At this point, four ghouls rush up the stairs and attack! Joe shoots one with his trusty Colt 1911 pistols, Rita bashes one with a baseball bat, and William manages to knock one down the stairs with his shovel. Daisy desperately tries to undo the magic that is preventing them from leaving - but before she can manage, two more ghouls rush down from upstairs. With the aid of Daisy's shriveling spell, the ghouls are finished off, and Daisy has time to undo the magic. The team step outside, only to face two more ghouls and a cackling ghoul priest. Joe and Daisy take up positions where they can shoot and cast spells remotely, while Rita and William go in swinging. After a pitched battle where Rita gets slightly wounded and Daisy is struck by horror, the ghouls are killed and the priest is defeated. He shrivels into a puddle of black goop, leaving behind a mysterious amulet. Friend or Foe? At this moment, Lita Chantler approaches, and tells the investigators more about the ghouls and that they are planning something for tomorrow night. She suggests burning down Joe's house, but Joe refuses. She plans to stop the ghouls' plan - and asks for help. The team decide they don't trust her and refuse, instead heading to Velma's diner to consult with Agnes Baker - a trusted friend of Joe. Agnes tells the investigators that will need to know three things to have a chance of stopping the cult: The location of the ritual Information of the ghouls' weaknesses Details of the ritual in order to disrupt it

docs.text: Hunger from Below So, What's the Plan? With the investigators fully prepped and ready for action, they drive to Arkham woods and set off to find the site of the ritual. Daisy has learned a new spell, and William and Joe have practiced their melee and ranged attack skills to fine art over the course of the day. Before the Finale Creeping into the woods, the investigators find the bent oak tree and discover a clearing just beyond. They hear a chorus of howls, and are overwhelmed but nausea when the smell of rotting flesh washes over them. They spy a crowd of ghouls dragging dead bodies and other flesh over to a hole and dropping it in. After a hurried discussion, the use of a Molotov cocktail is decided to be the best way to both kill a large number of ghouls and create a distraction so they they can sneak by and investigate the hole. The plan is a success, and they follow the faint sound of chanting down some stairs into the darkness. The Ritual As they reach the bottom of the stairs, the chanting reaches an unhinged crescendo. They see three abductees tied up, while a cult leader wearing mask made of a huge elk skull leads other cultists in a ceremony. A hurried discussion takes place to decide strategy - Lita and William sneak forward and take cover behind a couple of pillars. Daisy emerges into the chamber and casts a spell targeting the cult leader. He offers a simple trade. "Offer up the the betrayer of the Ancient One and you may leave this place unharmed - and you may take the other sacrifices with you." Joe is initially torn between sacrificing Lita to the ritual and fighting back, but Daisy makes a good case to convince him to come in guns blazing - which he does, knocking the cult leader over. The other cultists rush forward to attack, but Lita and William hold them off for a while. As Daisy and the cult leader cast spells at each other, tentacles emerge from the depths and start attacking - first spraying William with acid, and then grabbing him and Lita. Daisy and Joe manage to injure the cult leader so much that he falls into a coma, while Agnes quickly tries to free the abductees. Half the cultists are defeated, and Lita and William manage to break free of the tentacles just as the cult leader dies - triggering the chamber to start collapsing. Joe carries one abductee up the stairs, while Agnes convinces the others to run for their lives. Bursting free as the ground behind them collapses into itself, the investigators breathe a sigh of relief and take a moment to go over the events of the past day or so. They have foiled the cultists' plans, but have they made themselves a target for Umhôrdhoth?

"Offer up the the betrayer of the Ancient One and you may leave this place unharmed - and you may take the other sacrifices with you." Joe is initially torn between sacrificing Lita to the ritual and fighting back, but Daisy makes a good case to convince him to come in guns blazing - which he does, knocking the cult leader over. The other cultists rush forward to attack, but Lita and William hold them off for a while. As Daisy and the cult leader cast spells at each other, tentacles emerge from the depths and start attacking - first spraying William with acid, and then grabbing him and Lita. Daisy and Joe manage to injure the cult leader so much that he falls into a coma, while Agnes quickly tries to free the abductees. Half the cultists are defeated, and Lita and William manage to break free of the tentacles just as the cult leader dies - triggering the chamber to start collapsing. Joe carries one abductee up the stairs, while Agnes convinces the others to run for their lives. Bursting free as the ground behind them collapses into itself, the investigators breathe a sigh of relief and take a moment to go over the events of the past day or so. They have foiled the cultists' plans, but have they made themselves a target for Umhôrdhoth?

docs.text: The Last Train Scene 1: The Handoff Section D agent Garance de Winter has prepared documents and travel arrangements for herself, her driver Louis Lafite , and an another agent Calvin Crowfoot to travel to Vienna, where they are to meet up with Gisela Waltrun , a German intelligence officer who has unexpectedly contacted Section D asking to meet. Their handler Lieutenant Strang has instructed Garance to also transport a "package" of Piotr Wierzbicki and has arranged cover as "importers of machine parts" on a cargo train. A woman meets the agents at the station with Piotr, and seems slightly fearful of him. She hands him a small tin with and instruction of not to open, and then abruptly walks away. Garance takes Piotr under her wing and they settle themselves in on the train. Piotr is very taken with Louis' unusual dog, and the dog is also very interested in Piotr. Their container has some seating and small curtained off area for Piotr to sleep. As they travel, Piotr chats away merrily about his hobbies and his recent past. The agents note that he has a gap in his memory from about three weeks ago, where his father suddenly went missing. Since then, everyone has been telling him that things will be fine and he will see his father again soon. He repeatedly asks whether he can draw. When he starts drawing, he draws intricate vistas of strange alien architecture, with a recurring symbol. Calvin notices that the pictures he draws can be lined up next to each other to form a vista of a great city. Louis tries to take a close look at one of the drawings and accidentally drops it out a window. Piotr is furious . Scene 2: Border Crossing The initial journey is uneventful, and everyone sleeps reasonable well. At the border to Czechoslovakia the following morning, a customs patrol boards the train and makes their way through. When they reach the compartment with the agents, the officers are mostly indifferent, but one seems to take umbrage with Calvin and looks at his papers with more detail. He seems like he might raise an alarm, but Garance manages to charm him and they moves on. Piotr has been sitting still with his eyes closed for the whole time of the inspection, but when the train starts moving again he suddenly announces that "The man in the black coat already knows we are on the train." The agents are on edge, but nothing happens for some time. Then, after passing Bratislava, the lights suddenly go off in a tunnel. After ten seconds the lights come back on, but there is a symbol drawn in the condensation in the glass - the same as that in Piotr's drawings. Piotr appears to be asleep. Scene 3: The Search The train starts slowing down unexpectedly. The agents read the signal flags and determine that the train has been instructed to stop for a military inspection. They see some Nazi soldiers in black coats emerge from a troop carrier and head towards the back of the train, and a soldier and a commander head to the front. After a minimal delay, the train starts moving again. The agents have about fifteen minutes before the solders discover them assuming they are searching the train thoroughly. The agents notice that the soldiers are all wearing an armband with a strange symbol. Calvin heads up front and tries to overcome the two Nazis there. Louis heads back and tries to disengage the rear coaches so the soldiers are left behind. Louis is initially confused about how to disconnect the carriages, but then starts making progress. Calvin tries to ambush the soldiers in the engine, but does not manage to make a killing blow. Garance is staying with Piotr who is drawing a scene of a fight occurring in a train engine. Calvin takes out the lower-rank soldier - then the commander casts a spell at him, and is shocked when it fails utterly. The commander shoots, but his gun jams - then when attacking with his sword he is shot in the eye and then through the head. Meanwhile, Louis has almost managed to extract the pin that connects the carriages, but a soldier appears and shoots him at the last minute - but it's too late, and the rear coaches fall away as the train lurches forward. The train driver warns Calvin that the Nazis are setting up a blockage ahead, and that he will slow down at a corner ahead so they can jump off undetected. Scene 4: The Road to Vienna The agents and Piotr jump off the train as it slows. Calvin and Louis agree on the best way forward, and promptly lead everyone into a ditch. Eventually, they make their way to a road and after a forty minute walk they find Karl Hoffmann standing over his Opel Kapitan, trying to "fix" the engine by prodding it with various tools. Louis takes matters into his own hands and fixes the engine. Karl is delighted, and invites the agents to accompany him back to Vienna. He invites Louis to drive. He talks all the time about his business, his relations, the car, and many other topics. He noticeably avoids politics, which he finds distasteful. He mentions a party he attended at Count Erich Albrecht 's chateau and he is planning to go to another gathering there tonight. He mentions several of the attendees, and the fact that people share strange objects and perform rituals, which he takes as a joke. Piotr whispers to Garance "He has been in a room with them. He doesn't know." Scene 5: The Roadblock Karl directs Louis to take a shortcut, but is put out when they round a corner and find a small queue of vehicles in front of a small single-lane bridge - part of the parapet has collapsed and there is a crack in the approach slab. Amongst the waiting vehicles, a smart Mercedes staff car looks like it has someone important on board. Karl leaps out and starts handing out his business card to everyone present. Calvin clears the debris from the bridge and inspects the pillars. He gives a thumbs up, and the Mercedes zooms forward, obviously in a big rush. Scene 6: The Handover In Vienna, Karl drops them at their "hotel" and gives the agents some business cards. The agents make their way to the Section D safe-house, where they meet Professor Richard Deadman who takes charge of Piotr. The agents brief him, and he tells them the following: The staff car was owned by Hauptsturmfuhrer Vogel , a Nazi official in Black Sun . Black Sun is a cult that has aligned itself with the Nazi party, though it predates it. They are obsessed with occult rituals and arcane artifacts. The symbol that Piotr has been drawing has appeared in intercepted Black Sun communiques. It has also appeared in secret communiques of another Nazi faction - the Nachtwolfe . Nachtwolfe are a newer group and seem to favour advanced technology with some unknown power source. They are often at odds with Black Sun as they compete over ancient artifacts. Section D has been trying to find an "in" with Count Albrecht's esoteric parties, so the agents should try to attend if they can and report back. One of the attendees that Karl mentioned - Gotthold Fuchs - is a suspected Nachtwolfe agent. With two days to go until their meeting with Gisela, the agents contact Karl. He is in a panic and asks to meet in the park. There, he keeps inviting them to the party tonight and then telling them he is inviting them without wanting to. He is also missing some memories and has not slept. The agents decide to investigate.

docs.text: Reaching the Ice Scene 1: Job Interview Lucrecia received a telegram from Professor Dyer inviting her to come on his rescue expedition to Antarctica as a pilot. She eagerly agrees, and makes her way to Providence RI to join the crew. At the station, she is met by Jurgen Harkson , who greets her eagerly and drives her to the warehouse at the harbor. As she is crossing the yard and admiring the planes, they are met by Dean who seems to have joined the team due to his uncanny knack of improving engines in a way that defies science. Making their way to Dyer's office, they meet three more people who have just been interviewed and are joining the expedition - Leroy , Jose and Brock . In his office, they are also joined by Lynn Pabodie who is second-in-command and chief mechanic. They find out about the length of the trip and how much they will be paid. They meet some of the other members of the crew as they start their training. Leroy ends up befriending Lynn and talking about her engineering work at the university Jose bonds with Acacia Drakos over prior mercenary work Brock spends time with the ship's bosun Nguyen Ly where they discuss their former lives of crime Dean follows the explosives expert Marcus Blaine around - and is getting the uncanny feeling that this is a lot of explosives to be taking on a rescue mission Lucrecia ends up slightly enamored with the chief pilot Manuel Pereira Scene 2: The Society of Antediluvian Research Marcus, Acacia and two other military experts ( Nico Argyros and Maria Kastallanos ) invite the investigators to the Biltmore, a hotel that is openly a speakeasy. While drinking at a table, they are approached by Ms. Neiman , who introduces herself as a representative of the Society of Antediluvian Research. She offers everyone a two-month job for $500 each, which after some discussion the team refuse - after determining that the society almost never publishes academic papers or sponsors public research, and that Ms. Neiman is probably hiding something. They fail to convince Maria however, who decides to take her up on the offer. Scene 3: Danforth Returns Leroy is struggling to find his sea-legs, despite still being on land, so takes some time off. Meanwhile, after a meeting with the captain, Lucrecia and Brock notice a suspicious figure moving about the warehouse. Brock sneaks up and recognises Danforth, a former student of Dyer. They find bombs in his bag, and forcibly subdue him - handing him over to Dyer, the two of them have a heated argument about the safety of the expedition. Dyer sadly hands him over to the police, who decide to commit Danforth to the sanitarium. Unfortunately Danforth had already set a bomb, which goes off that night and destroys some of the food and some of the cyclonite charges. The ship - the Aurora - sets off with the investigators onboard, and they make a stop at Havana to pick up rum and cigars, then everyone undergoes a ceremony as they cross the equator - led by Bosun Nguyen and aided by Brock. Manuel expresses distrust of some members of the crew. Scene 4: Mount Erebus Arriving at Ross Island just off Antarctica, the crew and expedition start unpacking everything. After talking to Dyer, the investigators (minus Leroy) head out up to the top of Mount Erebus to see if they can see anything of the Delaware . Lucrecia struggles with the climb and injures herself. They spot the ship about 20 miles away, and decide to head back to the Aurora and take a motor launch there the next day. Scene 5: Wreck of the Delaware Arriving at the ship, they notice that it is listing and has taken on water. They also find several crates and a slightly damaged Hercules airplane lashed to the ice. Entering the ship, they find body parts and blood everywhere, as if something monstrous ripped the crew apart. Exploring further, they find the bodies of two crew members in the propellor shaft, with strange symbols carved into the bulkheads next to them. Scene 6: Tek-tek Horror The team is attacked by three Tek-Teks, which slash at them, injuring Lucrecia and causing some horror for everyone. As they are killed, they drop fragments of a stone tablet. Once the Tek-Teks are all killed, the investigators hear Tek-Tek noises coming from other parts of the ship. Jose decides to hunt them down, and once they have destroyed four more, they have all the pieces of the tablet. Putting it together and reading the inscription aloud, the tablet seals itself together and the black swirling mist around the pieces disappears. The team decide to throw the tablet into the Antarctic Ocean to avoid summoning more Tek-Teks. Scene 7: Reporting Back The team arrive back at the Aurora, and report their finding to Dyer, who is with Lynn and Jurgen. They all seem quite unfazed, almost as if they had been expecting something like this. Manuel reiterates their suspicions of a few of those aboard the Aurora. Scene 8: Finding the Starkweather-Moore Camp It takes a day to set up the planes. Dean heads off to try to repair the Hercules by the Delaware. Lucrecia pilots one of the planes, with the others helping to navigate. The first search is unsuccessful, and the team have to head back to the Aurora to refuel. On the second attempt, they spot the camp and land to explore. Scene 9: Exploring the Camp The camp looks like it has been attacked - a Hercules plane has its wing melted and bodies lie with limbs ripped off. Brock finds an expedition journal. Leroy and Jose think that between 10 and 20 bodies are unaccounted for. They also think that the deaths are very strange, with flesh being melted away leaving bone behind. Scene 10: Conference Captain Khatri wants to leave and head back home, but Dyer insists that they press on. The team help to convince everyone to stay and help. Scene 11: Sabotage! With everyone suspicious, the team decide to perform guard duty overnight. Brock and Jose take the first shift, which is quiet. Lucrecia and Leroy take the second, and as they are patrolling they see one of the planes go up in flames! Two of the member of the expedition and three members of the crew have petrol bombs and pistols! A fight breaks out, and a second plane is set alight - luckily Lucrecia manages to put out the flames before it is too damaged, but the first plane is destroyed. Brock and Jose emerge from the tents to help with the fight, and they kill most of the cultists. One last cultist is restrained and he is eventually intimidated into saying that the Society of Antediluvian Research is behind the attacks.
docs.title: Reaching the Ice

docs.text: Lucrecia received a telegram from Professor Dyer inviting her to come on his rescue expedition to Antarctica as a pilot. She eagerly agrees, and makes her way to Providence RI to join the crew. At the station, she is met by Jurgen Harkson , who greets her eagerly and drives her to the warehouse at the harbor. As she is crossing the yard and admiring the planes, they are met by Dean who seems to have joined the team due to his uncanny knack of improving engines in a way that defies science. Making their way to Dyer's office, they meet three more people who have just been interviewed and are joining the expedition - Leroy , Jose and Brock . In his office, they are also joined by Lynn Pabodie who is second-in-command and chief mechanic. They find out about the length of the trip and how much they will be paid. They meet some of the other members of the crew as they start their training. Leroy ends up befriending Lynn and talking about her engineering work at the university Jose bonds with Acacia Drakos over prior mercenary work Brock spends time with the ship's bosun Nguyen Ly where they discuss their former lives of crime Dean follows the explosives expert Marcus Blaine around - and is getting the uncanny feeling that this is a lot of explosives to be taking on a rescue mission Lucrecia ends up slightly enamored with the chief pilot Manuel Pereira
docs.title: Scene 1: Job Interview

docs.text: Marcus, Acacia and two other military experts ( Nico Argyros and Maria Kastallanos ) invite the investigators to the Biltmore, a hotel that is openly a speakeasy. While drinking at a table, they are approached by Ms. Neiman , who introduces herself as a representative of the Society of Antediluvian Research. She offers everyone a two-month job for $500 each, which after some discussion the team refuse - after determining that the society almost never publishes academic papers or sponsors public research, and that Ms. Neiman is probably hiding something. They fail to convince Maria however, who decides to take her up on the offer.
docs.title: Scene 2: The Society of Antediluvian Research

docs.text: Leroy is struggling to find his sea-legs, despite still being on land, so takes some time off. Meanwhile, after a meeting with the captain, Lucrecia and Brock notice a suspicious figure moving about the warehouse. Brock sneaks up and recognises Danforth, a former student of Dyer. They find bombs in his bag, and forcibly subdue him - handing him over to Dyer, the two of them have a heated argument about the safety of the expedition. Dyer sadly hands him over to the police, who decide to commit Danforth to the sanitarium. Unfortunately Danforth had already set a bomb, which goes off that night and destroys some of the food and some of the cyclonite charges. The ship - the Aurora - sets off with the investigators onboard, and they make a stop at Havana to pick up rum and cigars, then everyone undergoes a ceremony as they cross the equator - led by Bosun Nguyen and aided by Brock. Manuel expresses distrust of some members of the crew.
docs.title: Scene 3: Danforth Returns

docs.text: Arriving at Ross Island just off Antarctica, the crew and expedition start unpacking everything. After talking to Dyer, the investigators (minus Leroy) head out up to the top of Mount Erebus to see if they can see anything of the Delaware . Lucrecia struggles with the climb and injures herself. They spot the ship about 20 miles away, and decide to head back to the Aurora and take a motor launch there the next day.
docs.title: Scene 4: Mount Erebus

docs.text: Arriving at the ship, they notice that it is listing and has taken on water. They also find several crates and a slightly damaged Hercules airplane lashed to the ice. Entering the ship, they find body parts and blood everywhere, as if something monstrous ripped the crew apart. Exploring further, they find the bodies of two crew members in the propellor shaft, with strange symbols carved into the bulkheads next to them.
docs.title: Scene 5: Wreck of the Delaware

docs.text: The team is attacked by three Tek-Teks, which slash at them, injuring Lucrecia and causing some horror for everyone. As they are killed, they drop fragments of a stone tablet. Once the Tek-Teks are all killed, the investigators hear Tek-Tek noises coming from other parts of the ship. Jose decides to hunt them down, and once they have destroyed four more, they have all the pieces of the tablet. Putting it together and reading the inscription aloud, the tablet seals itself together and the black swirling mist around the pieces disappears. The team decide to throw the tablet into the Antarctic Ocean to avoid summoning more Tek-Teks.
docs.title: Scene 6: Tek-tek Horror

docs.text: The team arrive back at the Aurora, and report their finding to Dyer, who is with Lynn and Jurgen. They all seem quite unfazed, almost as if they had been expecting something like this. Manuel reiterates their suspicions of a few of those aboard the Aurora.
docs.title: Scene 7: Reporting Back

docs.text: It takes a day to set up the planes. Dean heads off to try to repair the Hercules by the Delaware. Lucrecia pilots one of the planes, with the others helping to navigate. The first search is unsuccessful, and the team have to head back to the Aurora to refuel. On the second attempt, they spot the camp and land to explore.
docs.title: Scene 8: Finding the Starkweather-Moore Camp

docs.text: The camp looks like it has been attacked - a Hercules plane has its wing melted and bodies lie with limbs ripped off. Brock finds an expedition journal. Leroy and Jose think that between 10 and 20 bodies are unaccounted for. They also think that the deaths are very strange, with flesh being melted away leaving bone behind.
docs.title: Scene 9: Exploring the Camp

docs.text: Captain Khatri wants to leave and head back home, but Dyer insists that they press on. The team help to convince everyone to stay and help.
docs.title: Scene 10: Conference

docs.text: With everyone suspicious, the team decide to perform guard duty overnight. Brock and Jose take the first shift, which is quiet. Lucrecia and Leroy take the second, and as they are patrolling they see one of the planes go up in flames! Two of the member of the expedition and three members of the crew have petrol bombs and pistols! A fight breaks out, and a second plane is set alight - luckily Lucrecia manages to put out the flames before it is too damaged, but the first plane is destroyed. Brock and Jose emerge from the tents to help with the fight, and they kill most of the cultists. One last cultist is restrained and he is eventually intimidated into saying that the Society of Antediluvian Research is behind the attacks.

docs.text: A Phantom of Truth The first night After a restless night and dreams of the events so far, the investigators resolve to travel to Paris to try to find Nigel Engram , the mysterious producer of the play. Arriving at the Gare D'Orsay the team head towards Montparnasse where they remembered a a cast member saying that they had met Nigel there in a cafe. Heading that way, they hear discordant organ music coming from the Church of St. Barnabé. At a bar in the evening, they don't manage to gather any information about Nigel, but they do encounter people talking about strange symbols that have been drawn on nearby buildings, which look uncannily like the Yellow Sign that that have encountered elsewhere, including on the onyx amulet that they "borrowed" from the historical society in Arkham. Heading to the Gardens of Luxembourg they find a statue holding the symbol, and footprints heading toward Notre Dame - however they are being watched by creatures above them. At this moment, the organ music they heard earlier starts echoing inside their head, and a mysterious figure with deathly pale skin dressed all in black approaches them. They manage to find a passage that is not watched and make a run for it. At Notre Dame they search around but don't find anything of significance. The organ music echoes inside their head, and the mysterious figure approaches again. Wisely deciding to retreat, the team head to La Marais and then on to Père Lachaise Cemetery, where they are ambushed by a trio of Byakhees. After killing them, the figure accompanied by the mysterious piping appears again, but the team manage to evade him and at that moment dawn breaks, giving some respite. A gravestone gives a hint that the Engram family may be found in the west of the city. The second night Having some time to patch up some wounds, the team then head to the Canal Saint-Martin where they find an old plaque that references some hidden Catacombs under Paris. Joe finds a hidden passage which enables them to evade the organist again. Making a beeline for Montmartre, they find a late night cafe. With a bit of prompting, a member of the clientele has heard of Nigel Engram and says he has connections to the Grand Guignol theatre. At the theatre, they catch the end of a play on the topic of insanity. After the show, the cast and audience are happy to discuss the issues raised, and happen to mention that Nigel has a house by the Opera Garnier. However, at this moment The Stranger appears. William manages to talk to him (though he does not respond), and which moment the investigators are startled by a noise behind them - the cast and audience are gone, and three cultists have appeared, and the Stranger has disappeared. A fight ensues, and the cultists are defeated, with two of the three dying from Daisy's spells. Dawn breaks and the team has a brief rest, though the sound of organ music never fully leaves them. The third night Heading to the Opera Garnier, the investigators are disturbed to see the doors open, a fine mist covering the ground, and most disturbingly a trail of blood leading up the steps. Deciding to make a final stand here, they decide to set traps. Rita has a moment of inspiration and decides to try playing the opera house's pipe organ, which she is relieved to discover seems to counteract some of the stress of the discordant organ music ringing in her head. When the organist enters, the plan is put into action. An antique lamp on a rope swing down and hits him, and then William swings down and stabs him. These actions seem to baffle him rather than damage him, but they do slow him down. He does seem rather more disconcerted by the organ music that Rita is playing. When William tries to put a straitjacket on him, he is indifferent - causing the jacket to decay into pieces and striding forward. He seems to only be slowed by music, so Joe And Daisy start singing - which is initially successful, but the organist quickly adapts so that it no longer affects him. Instead, they rush to the orchestra pit to try to find musical instruments to aid with Rita's work on the organ. They find a violin and a saxophone left behind and start to play along. At this point, William is terrified, and tries to run away - forgetting that he is tied to a rope. He does manage to cut himself free and escapes to the corner of the opera house, where he pulls out a harmonica. With the music playing, the organist is slowed enough that he barely reaches Rita before dawn breaks, and fails to destroy the minds of the investigators. At dawn, he disappears into mist, and the team make a break for it. By chance, they find Nigel Engram's house as they are escaping. They knock on the door. Nigel welcomes them into his house, and gives them cheese and biscuits. He also seems to have been expecting them - and seems excited that the investigators will find the path to Carcosa. On his table is a map of the secret catacombs below Paris. He steps into the kitchen to fetch the tea - however when Daisy follows him, she finds his body hanging from the ceiling fan, rotting from weeks of decomposition.

docs.text: Black Stars Rise The Tide Rises With a storm raging, the investigators dock at Porte de l'Avoncée and make their way up the hill. The road to the abbey looks blocked, so the team make their way round the outer wall to the north tower. With the rain making the going treacherous, William and Joe slip and hurt themselves just before a monster appears over the ramparts. However, Rita manages to pick the beast up after it was injured and throws it over the wall to land on the rocks far below. Gingerly making their way over some broken steps, a couple of cultists ambush the team, but again are defeated easily by the team. However when they approach the entrance to the abbey, a couple of Rift Seekers attack, which are a bit hardier. Rita breaks the wing of one and throws it at the other, and then Joe is shaken by the experience, but still manages to kill the second with his Tommy Gun. Let the Storm Rage Inside the abbey, the team are confronted by the Beast from Aldeberan - a tough fight in which Rita is injured, and Joe and William both are stricken with horror and have to run away before recovering. Once defeated, the investigators explore the abbey and find a lone monk who ushers them into a small room to wait for the abbot. As he disappears, the investigators search the room and find a key. After the monk does not reappear, the team head to the tower and unlock it. At the top, they find a group of four cultists performing a ritual to summon Hastur - Rita throws one over the side of the tower, and William and Joe shoot the others. Open the Path Below Rushing back down to the abbey, they see the monk again who has no recollection of seeing them before. Leaving him behind, the investigators head to the chapel of St. Aubert. William sees the image of Carcosa below the waves, and tries to steel himself to dive in to the water. He doesn't manage, but Joe and Rita take the plunge, dragging him along with them. The team emerge from the waters of Lake Hali and see the ruins of Carcosa in front of them.

docs.text: Curtain Call Awakening The investigators watch the first act of The King in Yellow and are confused by the meandering and slow-paced story. Falling asleep in the interval, they are surprised when they wake to find the rest of the audience dead and the decor is ripped, rotten and tattered. Not finding much in the auditorium itself, Joe leads the way to the foyer where they find the doors to the theatre seem to have been replaced with blank walls. Joe goes into the lighting booth and starts switching on lights - and sees movement in the shadows when he does. William and Daisy head up to the balcony, where William is pushed off into the auditorium below by a cultist in yellow robes. Another cultist appears in the auditorium at this point, and another in the doorway of the lighting booth. Daisy and Will deal with the two in the auditorium, and Joe expertly uses his dual-wielded pistols to take down the one in the booth. Stepping up on to the stage, a large tentacled monster appears, but the investigators appear to finish it off before it can cause too much harm - at least it vanishes into the shadows. Exploring backstage, they hear a banging and cries for help from one of the rooms. Lola Hayes who played Cassilda in the play is trapped inside, telling the investigators that the actor who plays The Stranger (played by The Man in the Pallid Mask ) changes for every performance, and sometimes between rehearsals. She tells them that he never takes his mask off, and that when he stared at her during the interval she blacked out - awaking to find herself locked in the dressing room which has become rotted and terrifying. Daisy finds a tattered yellow robe in the room, and decides to put it on. Looking out the door, she notices a shadow moving along the corridor. The Stranger The investigators and Lola rush along the corridor and see a shadow move into the rehearsal room (which has a strange symbol carved into the wall). Daisy confronts the Man in the Pallid Mask there, who gives the impression of laughing behind the mask. He is backed into the corner of the room, but at that moment, there is a crash and a wave of searing heat. The investigators turn to see that the auditorium is on fire - but when they turn back, the man is gone. Rushing back towards the front of the theatre, the monster reappears, along with three cultists. The monster attacks William, who manages to hold it off while Daisy manages to incapacitate it. Meanwhile, Lola is engages with one cultist and Joe tries to escape but is cornered by the other two while the fire begins to surround him. Joe manages to expertly yank the two cultists into the fire and escape himself, while Lola blinds the monster and the remaining cultist in order to reach the foyer at the same time. Standing by the wall where the doors to the outside used to be, The Man in the Pallid Mask watches the investigators approach. Joe opens fire on him and seems to hurt him. His disturbing visage and mannerisms quickly cause horror and panic among the team, and with the fire rapidly catching up to them things are looking grim. However Joe manages another one-two shot which hits the mask - which disturbingly does not drop away or appear damaged. At this moment, the man bows and opens a glass door leading outside, disappearing through it. With the theatre about to collapse, the investigators rush through and flee for a couple of blocks. Encore Deciding not to go to the police, the team backtrack to see what has happened to the theatre. They are confused to see it standing with its exterior looking the same as it did before the play started. Daisy feels like she is being watched, and turning round she sees the man in the pallid mask standing on the sidewalk. He turns and disappears into the alley behind the theatre. Giving chase, the team find nothing except a poster invitation to the cast party, at the home of Constance Dumaine .

docs.text: Echoes of the Past Race for Answers Tonight's performance of "The King in Yellow" was not the first Arkham had seen. Daisy Walker ducks out at Velma's Diner to try to get her hair cut, and the rest of the team travel to the Arkham Historical Society to try to find out more. They arrive to find the front doors cracked halfway open and light streaming out. Opening the door to one of the record offices, they find numerous filing cabinets - all of which have been covered with a layer of thick black sludge. Deciding to leave this room alone, they move next to the meeting room. William finds an old lamp under the table, while Joe uses his investigative powers to deduce the hole in the ceiling was probably made by a sledgehammer. Rita denies that it was made by her, and has a relaxing cup of coffee while she watches the others do their stuff. Moving through into a large museum room with exhibits about Arkham's past, they find an old knife that William decides is very useful - but at that moment they hear a whispering voice echo through the building and all the electrical lights shatter. Luckily William still has his kerosene lamp and leads the way - but everyone hears the sound of movement in the floor above. Going upstairs, the team interrupt two cultists who are rummaging in the library. They are quickly dispatched, and a search of their bodies leads to Rita finding reference to a "secret" library somewhere. In the reading room next to the library, they find a record pertaining to the "dreadful events" surrounding the closure of the Cedar Playhouse. A note attached to the record states that the matter is too ghastly for the public eye, and that the full records are found in the hidden library. Mistakes of the Past The front door of the manor opens and then slams shut. The investigators hear a scared voice exclaiming that they don't know where the door is. Another voice responds with "You spoke the oath. You spoke his name." The first voice stammers "No! I cannot!" before his voice becomes distorted and cuts off. Wet footsteps start coming up the stairs. Rita stands at the top of the stairs and hits the monster that appears with her sledgehammer, while Joe shoots it. William then stabs it and pushes it down the stairs. The monster shakes its head and appears to heal all damage and injuries to it, then starts climbing the stairs again. Again, it is shot, smashed and stabbed, and again it recovers. At this point, William smashes his kerosene lamp against it forcing it back behind a wall of flame, where it appears to wait for the flames to die down. With a couple of minutes leeway, the investigators rush upstairs where they see light coming from one of the rooms. Rushing in they grab a couple of desks and quickly move them out to barricade the stairs, above the confused protestations of Mr. Peabody , the historical society curator. The Oath Joe tries to spin him a tall tale about what is going on, but Mr. Peabody does not seem convinced until William tells him what they need - access to the hidden library. Mr. Peabody says that he did know of some record on secret passages in the building, but he would have to look at the record to find out for sure. In the records room on the top floor, they find four more cultists rummaging for clues - Rita ambushes one, while Joe and William attack two more. Unfortunately, this fight does not go well for the team, with William and Rita picking up injuries from the fight and both running away scared at one point. Luckily Joe managed to finish off the last cultist, giving Mr. Peabody the time to search for the record he needed. He locates the secret latch that opens the way to the hidden library, and the team find the information they need - along with a mysterious onyx clasp with an alien inscription which the team decide to keep. The last record about "The King in Yellow" they find relates to a stagehand Daniel Chesterfield , who lost his wits after the final show. He was admitted to the asylum after the production ended. Perhaps he's still there...

Rita denies that it was made by her, and has a relaxing cup of coffee while she watches the others do their stuff. Moving through into a large museum room with exhibits about Arkham's past, they find an old knife that William decides is very useful - but at that moment they hear a whispering voice echo through the building and all the electrical lights shatter. Luckily William still has his kerosene lamp and leads the way - but everyone hears the sound of movement in the floor above. Going upstairs, the team interrupt two cultists who are rummaging in the library. They are quickly dispatched, and a search of their bodies leads to Rita finding reference to a "secret" library somewhere. In the reading room next to the library, they find a record pertaining to the "dreadful events" surrounding the closure of the Cedar Playhouse. A note attached to the record states that the matter is too ghastly for the public eye, and that the full records are found in the hidden library.
docs.title: Race for Answers

docs.text: The front door of the manor opens and then slams shut. The investigators hear a scared voice exclaiming that they don't know where the door is. Another voice responds with "You spoke the oath. You spoke his name." The first voice stammers "No! I cannot!" before his voice becomes distorted and cuts off. Wet footsteps start coming up the stairs. Rita stands at the top of the stairs and hits the monster that appears with her sledgehammer, while Joe shoots it. William then stabs it and pushes it down the stairs. The monster shakes its head and appears to heal all damage and injuries to it, then starts climbing the stairs again. Again, it is shot, smashed and stabbed, and again it recovers. At this point, William smashes his kerosene lamp against it forcing it back behind a wall of flame, where it appears to wait for the flames to die down. With a couple of minutes leeway, the investigators rush upstairs where they see light coming from one of the rooms. Rushing in they grab a couple of desks and quickly move them out to barricade the stairs, above the confused protestations of Mr. Peabody , the historical society curator.
docs.title: Mistakes of the Past

docs.text: Joe tries to spin him a tall tale about what is going on, but Mr. Peabody does not seem convinced until William tells him what they need - access to the hidden library. Mr. Peabody says that he did know of some record on secret passages in the building, but he would have to look at the record to find out for sure. In the records room on the top floor, they find four more cultists rummaging for clues - Rita ambushes one, while Joe and William attack two more. Unfortunately, this fight does not go well for the team, with William and Rita picking up injuries from the fight and both running away scared at one point. Luckily Joe managed to finish off the last cultist, giving Mr. Peabody the time to search for the record he needed. He locates the secret latch that opens the way to the hidden library, and the team find the information they need - along with a mysterious onyx clasp with an alien inscription which the team decide to keep. The last record about "The King in Yellow" they find relates to a stagehand Daniel Chesterfield , who lost his wits after the final show. He was admitted to the asylum after the production ended. Perhaps he's still there...

docs.text: The Last King Fashionably Late Constance Dumaine is hosting a party - but the investigators are met at the door by a path of blood, discordant music, and a doorman with only bloody stumps where he should have hands. Exploring the courtyard, the team are attacked by two nightgaunts who where perching on the rooftops. After defeating them, the team go through to the dining room, where they are confronted by the smell of rancid and rotten food. They interview Sebastien Moreau , who tells them that he has produced this show in Paris, Florence, New York - and that this was not the first production of "The King in Yellow" to be performed in Arkham. The Terrifying Truth Sebastien's passionate response seems to change his body, as fur sprouts and bulbous growths appear and his muscles bulge. He attacks the investigators, who quickly subdue him. Moving in to the ballroom so that Daisy can do a spot of dancing, Ashleigh Clarke is singing a song from the play about Lost Carcosa which mesmerizes the team. She follows this with a piercing shriek as her skin tightens hideously around her bones and insects start to eat there way out of her arms and shoulders. The investigators attack her and manage to overcome her. In the foyer again, the team meet Constance, who is confused and insulted when Daisy accuses her of hosting monsters and killers. She relates how the director Nigel Engram made everyone swear some sort of Oath before the rehearsals started. She laughs as the skin begins to fall off her body. Once again, the team subdue her. In the living room, they find the financier Jordan Perry sitting on the sofa smoking a cigar. The investigators manage to convince him to invest in Rita's education and he donates some money to the team. He ruminates on the fact that not every investment is about capital gain, and he was convinced by Nigel Engram to do the same for the play. As he puffs on his cigar, his body swells and his skin begins to harden and crack - with smoke issuing forth. The temperature in the room rises, and he attacks the investigators. Once he is defeated, the costume designer Ishimaru Huruko enters the room. She tells the team about the time she saw the 'Stranger' drawing a symbol. She recreates it for the team, and as she finishes it, her spine grows and extends upwards separating her torso from the bottom half of her body. At this moment the Stranger also appears. The investigators defeat them both, and decide this is an opportune moment to leave the party. Reality's Shadow As the team leaves, they are surprised to see that the front yard is now clean, the windows not smashed, and the soothing tones of slow jazz drifting out from the courtyard. They decide that things have calmed down and that they should go back to investigate what happened. All signs of the struggles and oddities have vanished, but as they enter the dining room, they see the Stranger speaking with a tall mustached man holding a silver-handled cane. The team run from the house in a haze of pain and disorientation. At this point, they feel they need to gear up, so they drive to the docks to meet with Jimmy "the Rat" and buy a Tommy gun and a sledgehammer.
