docs.text: The Pallid Mask Through the Catacombs With the partial map of the secret catacombs under Paris in hand, the investigators grab some torches and lanterns and head for the entrance. Once in the catacombs, they see the Man in the Pallid Mask beckon them forward and then disappear into the shadows. The investigators try to follow. but find themselves in a labyrinth of winding tunnels and chambers, with chattering skulls lining the walls. In an arched passageway, they are ambushed by ghouls - but these are quickly defeated. In another chamber, they find Dr. Thierry Henry (who Daisy recognises) who seems to be enchanted or possessed in some way and he is studying some carvings on the wall of one chamber. The team are also attacked by a disfigured humanoid enemy, but again manage to defeat it without to many issues. Unfortunately William is hypnotised by the Well of Souls, and drops his bowie knife down into it. It falls a long, long way before he hears a noise of it striking the bottom. Daisy and Joe are getting disturbed by the thought of something following them. Eventually the team find the Man in the Pallid Mask in the Tomb of Shadows, where he appears to be gesturing at the writing on the wall. The Path is Barred The team decide to take the time to try to understand what he is doing, and the Man in the Pallid Mask takes something from the fire to help him cast shadows in particular ways upon the wall, revealing a strange diagram. The shadows combine into an image of a building with a tall tower. with the spire reaching up to the ceiling. He beckons for the investigators to follow, and then disappears through the archway back into the catacombs. The Spectre of Death now catches up with the team, and starts to attack. The team manage to hold it off, and then Rita comes up with a plan to shove it down the Well of Souls - and succeeds! With the Spectre now out of the picture for now, the team hurry on. Leading the Way In a bone-filled cavern, more ghouls are dispatched with ease, and Willian manages to find a hatchet that manages to adequately replace his knife. Crawling through a small tunnel (and pulling Daisy with them after she got stuck), the investigators find a dead-end. The Stranger holds the skull that he pulled from the fire aloft, and the floor collapses into a dark pit. The Stranger bows, and falls backwards into the pit. The investigators jump in after him. Visions of two skylines, one above and one below, appear. One is of Mont Saint-Michel, and the other a warped reflection. This could be where the passageway between realities can be found. Waking up in the streets of Paris, the team decide to make their way to the coast to investigate.

docs.text: The Unspeakable Oath Locked Inside The investigators stop off at The Olde Curiosity Shoppe for Daisy to pick up an amulet of protection. Arriving at Arkham Asylum, they are welcomed by the receptionist who listens to their story about the King in Yellow and tells them that Daniel Chesterfield is in patient confinement and is only to be seen by medical staff under the direction of Dr. Mintz. Going in to the asylum, the doors are locked behind them and they turn to find that the receptionist has disappeared. Going into a staff room, Daisy and Rita find some doctors' white coats and decide to put them on. Rita also picks up a mug of coffee. The other patients do not respond to questioning and avoid the team, until two of them with a yellow gleam in their eyes attack. The investigators defeat them, and then head towards the infirmary. There they find a nurse who is very upset that Daisy and Rita have stolen staff uniforms, and when Daisy tries to claim that they are members of staff, she asks security to come in, and they restrain Daisy in a straitjacket and ask her to calm down. Rita takes this opportunity to steal the keys from nurse's belt. After they leave the infirmary, Rita helps Daisy out of the straitjacket. Tortuous Descent Unlocking the basement door, the team head down into the patient confinement area, where they find six cells. One cell contains a fit-looking middle aged man pacing around with a rictus grin permanently on his face. Another cell contains a women muttering about the guards, but the team can't make much sense of it. Two other cells contain old patients lying down, and one cell Joe is shocked to discover is empty but has his own handwriting on the wall mapping the way out. The last cell contains Daniel. The team free him, and when he sees the onyx amulet that was recovered from the Historical Society, he rants about Nigel Engram making them speak the Oath. "We spoke His name and the price was paid! Hastur! Hastur! O King!" Calming him down a little, the team think they might be able to get more information out of him if they leave the asylum, so they start to plot a way to escape. They are briefly delayed by a monster coming down the stairs, but kill it before it gets a chance to attack them. No Asylum After a brief realisation that all the investigators are starting to see the symbol from the onyx amulet (the Yellow Sign ) everywhere, the team set loose the grinning man - who they convince to go to the infirmary to cause trouble. Rita rushes off to light a fire in the kitchen to cause a distraction, while Daisy, William, and Joe start a fight in the yard. Several possessed patients attack, and the investigators defeat them. Unlocking the gate to the garden, they are confronted with a strange beast emerging from the trees. Rita runs to the outside gate, but it is locked and none of the keys on the nurse's keyring fit. At this moment, she remembers that she had a lock-pick tucked away and recovers it from inside her jacket. With the others holding the beast off, she picks the lock on the gate and everyone flees with Daniel in tow. Lost Soul Over a couple of days, the investigators manage to calm Daniel down, and he tells them that the King in Yellow is not just a play - it is a being named Hastur . He warns them not to say his name, and that the cultists are trying to find Carcosa to release Hastur from his prison. He asks the investigators to find the path before them, and seal Hastur for good. After coming back from a walk, the investigators find Daniel dead - choked to death. They decide to heed his warning, and start to work out how to get to Paris - where they believe Nigel Engram could be found.

docs.text: Mission 1: Dying to Meet You Scene 1: A Note from an Old Friend The agents arrive in Alexandria after being posted there by Section M. They equip themselves with some local weapons, and settle in to the city by browsing the street vendors. James receives a note from an old friend - Aisha Aziz - asking to meet him in The Rose of the Desert, a well known tea-shop. Asking around, they find their way there, though Yuri suspects that they may be being followed. Scene 2: The Rose of the Desert At the team-shop, they meet Aisha and settle down in a booth and order tea, sweets, and a hookah. As the conversation turns to more important business, Aisha suddenly grabs her neck and falls over. As she dies, she says "The time of the ...theuban... the snake is nigh. Seek the ziggurat beyond the Oasis of the Veiled Moon. Find Bruce Taylor , the Australian... he can show you the way. Goodbye old friend... the Tooth have claimed me at last." Looking up, they see two snake-masked figures peering through an upper window. The agents chase after them. Scene 3: A Rooftop Pursuit The assassins have a head start, but the agents catch up with them after getting tangled in some clothes, though some heavies also appear to support the masked figured. JJ falls asleep. Fighting the first assassin, they try to take him alive, but he bites down on something and dies immediately. The remaining assassin makes a break for a ship in the dock and makes it onboard. Scene 4: The Dhow Reaching the ship, the agents find more heavies and cultists defending it. As they fight, JJ runs below deck where he knocks over an oil lamp and catches the dhow on fire. He also finds some explosives which he takes with him. On the boat above, the fight is won by the agents. With JJ coming back up and warning about the fire, they quickly explore the captain's cabin and find a hidden note - "Brothers and sisters of the Serpent's Tooth. Aisha Aziz must die! I have discovered that she is a member of the cursed Alnim. Eliminate her before she can inform others of her discovery. Your Father, the Beloved of Yig"

docs.text: Mission 3: Oasis of the Veiled Moon Scene 1: Cairo Arriving at the docks, Yuri powers his way through the crowd, the others following him. Eva has a personal item stolen by a local urchin, but James chases after them and gets the item back. Bruce says he needs to collect a bag, and gives them instructions to get supplies, camping gear, camels and a guid, and to meet before dawn the next morning. Heading to the local Section M HQ, they meet up with the Quartermaster and JJ convinces them to part with some restricted weapons - three Blevins Enzymatic guns and a Blessed Kukri. They also suggest Chuma Salah as a possible guide and caravan leader, who the agents contact. JJ negotiates a good deal for them, and they start the journey as the sun rises. After a few hours, Salah spots a sandstorm. The agents decide to hunker down and sit out the storm. After it blows itself out, they carry on. That evening, a group of armed men approach and are unwilling to allow foreigners to pass in the current holy time. JJ manages to convince them of their good intentions and ability to deal with any problems, and they are allowed to pass. The next evening, they find a clump of petrified trees, and Bruce cried out "That's it!" He floors the accelerator and closes his eyes. Yuri manages to steer him camel through the anomaly, but Eva and Cieron are thrown off and have to drag their camels through. They see two pools, with some trees with hundreds of falcons resting on them. Scene 3: Battle of the Oasis Just before dawn, the agents are woken by deafening screeching. The falcons soar from their perches, forming a dark cloud, writhing and twisting. Individual birds break from the group and dive at the agents, swerving and flying off south and west before rising to join the throng. Salah runs to check on the camels, and Bruce heads to the north-east. The agents spot cultists crawling towards them, and Cieron opens fire on them. Their leader Shihaab al-Abdalla strides forward and casts a spell to bind the agents with tendrils of black smoke. He also has two enormous horned vipers with him, which set about attacking the agents. Yuri escapes, and chops one of the vipers in half, but is then charmed by Shihaab and is enthralled. Cieron and Eva are hurt badly. One of the cultists goes to chop Yuri's head off, but a mysterious shot rings out and the cultist falls dead. Bruce returns and starts firing, and an explosion erupts from where he went. Things are looking bad when more cultists appear, but at that moment a vortex of sand appears and encompasses the cultists, scouring the skin from their bodies. They make a panicked retreat, sacrificing themselves to protect Shihaab. With the cultists driven away, the vortex forms various faces and tries to communicate with the agents - Eva succeeds, and is healed by this spirit known as Bo-Ha-Bo , who then returns to her rest.

docs.text: The Caravanserai of a Thousand Fragrant Sighs Crossroads Heading in to the Caravanserai in the morning, the agents start to look around and trade with the locals. Yuri makes conversation with one of the food vendors, who tells of the legends saying that Alexander the Great founded the caravanserai and had a vision here of conquering this world and many others. James spots Serpent's Tooth cultists moving about and sometimes watching them. At their camp that night, Eva's koala leads them to a mysterious building in the caravanserai, where they see a cultist put his pendant in a special lock and enter a hidden door. The koala then warns them as a large number of Serpent's Tooth cultists and assassins drop down from the rooftops around them. The battle is tough, with the sheer number of cultists threatening to overwhelm the agents - however as more cultists arrive, the agents are rescued by a new group who quickly despatch the Serpent's Tooth. Their leader introduces herself as Nabila Daher , a friend of Aisha and a leader amongst the Order of the Alnim - the Order of the Mongoose - founded many centuries ago to oppose the Serpent's Tooth and their Ophidian masters. They accompany her to her caravan where they are healed and fed. She tells the agents that the cultists' activities has drastically increased recently, and that they may be performing some kind of ritual tonight - a perfect opportunity to infiltrate and catch them by surprise. What Slithers Below Dahir and four of her associates come with the agents to the door that the cultists used earlier, and used a serpent pendant to open it. Inside they find a storeroom, with a recess that fits another pendant. Putting this in opens a secret wall and a staircase leads down. Exploring the underground maze, the agents find some cultists training and decide to leave them alone. In one chamber portcullises slam down, but JJ picks the lock apart easily and they escape. In another chamber, they find a Gryphon chained to the wall and chomping on some dead goats. Eva befriends it somewhat, and everyone else sneaks through as she keeps it entertained. They hear some more cultists laughing and gambling and decide to sneak past them. At a large library, they find a copy of In the Macedon's Footsteps tome along with other old documents that Nabila takes with her. At the far end of the library, they hear chanting coming from behind a wall. Eva works out that the symbols on the wall represent planets, and she presses them in the correct order on the second attempt, opening up another secret door and a passage beyond. The Serpent's Lair At the entrance to a huge chamber, the agents peek in. Inside, there is a large dais with Shihaab al-Abdalla performing a complex ritual on it. To one side, they see Alom Shallar with her retinue of Ophidians. Other cultists are bringing ritual materials from a room in the rear. About fifty other cultists are present in the room. After a hasty tactical discussion, JJ decides to throw a bomb onto the dais. This knocks Shihaab back and disrupts the ritual - Alom Shallar retreats down a passageway with her companions, collapsing it behind her. The chamber starts to shake as Yig displays his wrath, and pieces of stone from the ceiling start tumbling down. Shihaab is furious and attacks with as much magic as he can muster. Yuri attacks back with his axe, and eventually Shihaab falls down. At that moment, several cultists grab his body and make a break for an exit, and the agents start running to escape as well. After a few hair-raising moments, they emerge into the night only to find the caravanserai collapsed behind them. Luckily the Alnim caravan was further away near the oasis, so the team heads there to get some rest. After a night's rest, Nabila discusses the tome and documents that they found. It's clear that the tome contains crucial information on the location of the Temple of Stars, where Alexander the great hid the Sceptre of Yig that he won after battling the Ophidians. Dahir agrees to guide them to the Forsaken Tomb, which supposedly shows the way to the Temple. With Dahir and some other members of the Alnim to accompany them, the agents take camels and supplies for two days march. On the third morning of travel, Dahir points to a hill where the Forsaken Tomb should sit - but the hilltop is empty. When they climb up, they see on the other side a massive temple structure that has risen from the sands, with a swirling sandstorm surrounding it.

docs.text: The Great Waste The Uncaring Desert That night, the team recover from their woes as much as they can, and prepare for the hike across the desert. They butcher the camels and prepare the meat, and gather enough food and water for three days. They also fashion backpacks out of the saddlebags after a couple of attempts. Deciding where to go, they realise that the Black Sun journal mentioned a Caravanserai about 45 miles west of their current location, which also seems to be a base for the Serpent's Tooth. They decide to set off in the early morning. The Deep Desert Day One Going is fairly easy in the morning across the sand, meaning the agents make good progress. At one point they see some Italian planes approaching, and they manage to find cover before they are shot at too much. They settle down for the night in a camp. Day Two The next day the agents find themselves on some hard pan, which offers some quicker going. At one point they spot a herd of game, and with some quick thinking they shoot some and spend some time butchering them. This provides extra rations in case they take longer to get to their destination. Day Three Entering some dry wash, the agents find a small stream, which they use to fill up their water containers. The canyons become a maze, but with some excellent navigation they find their way through and make camp again. Day Four As they are nearing the end of their journey, the agents are unfortunate to encounter a Black Sun squad in a truck. The troopers get out and open fire, and the Black Sun Dämonenbändiger summons his bonded Teufelshund . It is a hard battle, with several agents going down injured, but eventually they overcome the Black Sun. They take the truck and drive the last few miles to the Caravanserai of a Thousand Fragrant Sighs, where they camp by the oasis to recover.

docs.text: Mission 4: The Ziggurat of Alom Shallar Journey to the Sands The agents reach the Singing Sands, where Salah wishes them well and leaves them. The sands are bloody red, and keening cries drift over the dunes. Bruce and the agents all plug their ears and carry on. Camping that night, Yuri and Eva take the first watch, where they are attacked by snakes made of sand. Yuri wakes James, who shoots his tent in panic. After a while, the sand snakes recede. Obsidian Past The rest of the journey is quiet, except the hissing sound that follows them as they travel through the sands. After several hours, the agents see a 50m tall ziggurat framed against the afternoon sun. It appears to be made entirely of obsidian. They see several destroyed black sun vehicles outside, as well as a sacrificed body, which they think might have been part of a ritual to raise the ziggurat from the sands. JJ translates the carved words above the entrance, which read " Alom Shallar . Her prison and her tomb. Let none disturb her confinement. Let death take them." Entering the ziggurat, the door suddenly closes behind them. They make their way further in, and find an antechamber with vast bas-reliefs made of marble. Eva manages to interpret what is happening. Alom Shallar was born into a noble family, but one of her ancestors lost the Sceptre of Yig to Alexander the Great, leading to their house being disgraced. As a child, she showed great sorcerous power and was inducted into the Order of Yig. She rose through the ranks, and grew in ambition and power. She plotted to overthrow the Serpent Empress, but was captured along with her retinue. They are imprisoned within this obsidian ziggurat, which was sunk beneath the sands. Cieron touches a wet part of the bas-relief, which then lashes out at everyone there. The Corpse Show It takes them some time to find their way through the maze, as inside it is part illusion. Eventually they find the main chamber - four large statues of Alom Shallar surround a shattered jade sarcophagus. Everywhere there are parts of dead bodies, and every surface is covered in blood and viscera. The agents find a camera mounted on a tripod pointed at the sarcophagus. They find a projector in an alcove, and hastily set it up to watch the film. Six Black Sun Canons gather around the sarcophagus, arms raised and chanting. Troopers are also nearby holding guns raised. A tumult of power spreads from the Canons to the sarcophagus. The sarcophagus lid explodes outwards, shattering as it does so and shearing three of the Canons into pieces. Alom Shallar emerges, and the surviving Black Sun Canons speak to her, gesticulating wildly. She listens, then lazily moves her arm - the Canons are raised into the air and begin to come apart in a series of hideous bloody separations. A large formless shape scuttles up the wall onto the ceiling. Some troopers fire at it. The camera shows chunks of viscera and blood flying. Alom Shallar's retinue now also emerge. Alom Shallar moves towards the camera. As the film finishes, the dark formless shape drops from the ceiling. At that moment Bruce says a quick goodbye and seals the chamber behind him. The dark form - a Shuggonite - attacks, but as it is already injured the agents finish it off without too much trouble. They search around the chamber and find a notebook from the lead Black Sun Canon, and a way out through the ceiling. They make their way out, only to find Bruce gone with the truck, and all the camels shot in the head.

docs.text: Mission 2: Tobruk The agents spend a little time in the Alexandria library as Section M try to track down Bruce Taylor. They find various pieces of information and myths, including Serpent People or Ophidians have featured in many stories Millennia ago a vast serpent empire once covered the globe Sunken cities lay beneath the sand, waiting to be reawakened Several existing cults like the Children of Typhon and the Serpent's Tooth are known to be snake worshipers of a snake god known as Yig Back at Section M, Captain Brenda Andresson tells you that Bruce has been found - in Tubruk, currently besieged by Italian troops. Flying and boating in are not options, but a New Zealand long range desert patrol is heading that way and can drop you off nearby. Scene 1: A Drive Across the Sand A short hike out of Cairo, they are met by the Kiwis and their three modified patrol group vehicles. On the three-day journey, they are trained in desert survival. 125km out of Tubruk, they are stopped to refuel and hear the sound of a battle in the distance, along with a strange buzzing noise. When they arrive at the site of the battle, the victor has departed, leaving behind only mangled Italian soldiers and vehicles. Yuro thinks that the vehicles were destroyed by some sort of experimental weapon. They also spot a strange flat depression as something large moved around, but they lose the tracks when the ground becomes rocky. Scene 2: No Man's Land About 5km out of Tobruk, the agents say goodbye to the Kiwis who head off South. Under cover of darkness, the agents try to make their way into the city, timing their runs to avoid the searchlights. Luckily the Italians are not particularly vigilant, and they are more focussed on stopping anyone from coming out of the city. Unfortunately, Yuri steps on a mine - luckily JJ is on hand to disarm it for him. Reaching the outskirts of the city, they are confronted by some sceptical Australian troops, but manage to talk their way in. When they mention Bruce Taylor's name, the troops have mixed feelings about him: Always looking to make himself rich Known for locating items of dubious legality Smooth talker who normally manages to get himself out of trouble Caught "deserting" and is being held prisoner - he claims he was trying to "retrieve something for the good of the British Empire" but won't say what Scene 3: A Caged Bird Captain Foster hands Bruce over to the agents. Bruce says he knows how to get to the Oasis of Veiled Moon, and that he can guide them. Speaking with Captain Sullivan at the port, the agents request assistance in getting out of Tubruk. He has just the man in mind - Maloud is leaving in a few hours, and his dhow will fit them comfortably. Maloud confesses to be a collector of antiquities and oddities, and requests that the agents can pay him with some unusual artifacts in the future. At sea, a crewman calls to them that a U-boat has surfaced and is demanding they stop and prepare to be boarded. Maloud shrugs and says "I think I know the commander. Do not fire upon them - words are the best weapons. Now might be a good time to desert. You are deserters, right?" The Oberleutnant zer See introduced herself as Hannah Sarbruck . She chats to Maloud in Berber for several minutes, and seems amused to see the agents. Yuri notices a wolfhead badge on her collar, seemingly indicating that she may be a member of NachtWolfe. She bows to Maloud and leaves. Eventually, they reach Cairo without further incident.

It was a partial success, but his mind began to be taken over by Ithaqua. He returned to Arkham and paid someone to plant one idol in the Clover Club, then he planted one on a smuggling route used by the O'Bannions and let one be "captured" by Grady. The plan of Ithaqua and the Messenger seemed to be to find people who are not associated with Ithaqua to charge the onyx idol and help free his master. This may be because the onyx idol is a "key" used by the Ancient Ones when they were rumoured to have imprisoned Ithaqua after he rebelled. Having the onyx idol and the three wooden idols in one place was part of the plan, as the wooden idols drew beasts like wendigos close and the onyx idol then stole their spirit. docs.text: The Frozen Dead The Ritual Site Reaching the ritual site, the investigators take a look around - a crumbling stone circle in a snow-laden clearing, radiating an unnatural chill. They find the scorched remnants of a ritual fire, scattered silver coins, and clawed tracks leading away. Adelei discovers a ritual knife, blackened with dried blood. As they follow the tracks, three Cold Stalkers emerge from the nearby woods and attack. McG blasts one away with his Tommy gun, and Adelei manages to banish the other two. The Abandoned Lodge At the lodge, the team search for clues, initially finding a scrap of paper that indicating that Clarence was desperate to "bind the Wind-Walker’s favor" for the Sheldons. At this moment, they trigger a hidden ward carved into the lodge’s structure, and summon two spectral guardians known as Whispering Wraiths. Dan attacks with his machete as Adelei uses his banishment spell again to great effect, though he is also filled with terror and has to run into the corner of the room and hide. Luckily, there he finds Clarence’s journal which states that the ritual was incomplete, and he sought more power by summoning a Messenger of the Storm . Adelei thens takes this opportunity to perform a spell to gain a vision of Hyperborea - and is surprised to see Ithaqua communicating somehow with a tall spectral figure, which his vision shows is in a cave nearby. Meeting the Messenger The investigators trek to the cave, where they find jagged icicles and Hyperborean runes glowing faintly in the dark. Inside, the air is bitterly cold, and a constant wind howls through the tunnels. The walls are lined with strange carvings depicting figures bowing to a towering, faceless being. McG determines that the figures and probably making some kind of deal with the being and gaining powers in return for some favour. Further in, they find an altar covered in frost, surrounded by shattered silver coins and a faintly glowing black idol. The scene exudes an overwhelming sense of dread. As the investigators approach, a spectral figure materializes — the Messenger of the Storm, that Adelei saw in his vision. Initially the Messenger is pleased to see them, and mentions that they are now part of the Wind Walker's plan. It laments that the last people to come here were not strong enough, though they were used by binding their will to Ithaqua anyway. It thanks the investigators for returning the idols, and reaches forward to take them. Peter decides that this is a step too far, and opens fire on the Messenger, though it dodges out of the way. Adelei tries to banish it, and though the spell succeeds, the Messenger does enough to disrupt it - though it loses an arm in the process. Angered, it starts summoning Snow Wretches to aid it and causes snowstorms to blast the investigators, which knocks McG over. Adelei tries to banish it again, but finds that the spell fails. With everyone else attacking and injuring it, the Messenger starts to retreat and summon more Snow Wretches - but Peter finishes it off after Adelei blinds it. The team then make short work of the Snow Wretches. Adelei picks up the black idol - made from onyx and in a different style to the black wooden idols found so far - which is still glowing with some strange power. This triggers the cave to collapse - the investigators run for the exit with frozen stalactites falling and the walls cracking. They burst free from the entrance just as the whole cave implodes. Taking some time to recover, they then head back to the car. As they drive back, they try to decide how to study the idol and whether it should be used or destroyed.

docs.text: The Frozen Warning Blizzards have been plaguing Massachusetts. Some people are starting to suspect that something is amiss, because they have never been this fierce and unrelenting before. Rumours are starting to spread about voices on the wind - people are calling it the Whispering Frost - and some locals are disappearing without a trace. Supplies are running low, and the local gangs are using this opportunity to fill their coffers with supply work - both legal and illegal. Silent Signals Seamus O'Bannion has hired a couple of freelancers - the hitman Peter Gill and paranormal investigator McG - to help cook and supplier Adelei and enforcer Dan Pacho to recover some key supplies, bootlegged alcohol and some "extra items" that Grady Mills should have delivered. He is normally reliable, but he has gone strangely silent since his last message, which ended with a garbled "... the winds". Peter and Adelei test out driving the van, and both of them have trouble manoeuvering, but once they get on the road, Peter gets the hang of it. Which is lucky, because a fierce blizzard comes down suddenly about 45 minutes into the drive, and after hitting some ice on the road, he managed to stop the van from crashing, and instead drives it down a drive to an old barn, with the wind seeming to push them towards it. As he and Dan open the barn doors to get the van sheltered inside, McG investigates the barn. Picking up a strange black idol, McG hears whispers and sees a flash of a snow-covered wilderness where unnatural shapes stalk the landscape. Turning round to tell everyone else, a Cold Shadow emerges from the idol and attacks. The investigators manage to bring it down without too much trouble, and the blizzard outside seems to die down. Driving on to Grady's hideout, McG and Adelei examine the idol, and think it may have a connection to Ithaqua . The Howling Woods At the hideout, Peter and Dan go inside to investigate while McG and Adelei scout the perimeter. Inside, they find some notes and a map with the words "The Storm's Eye", and notice that it is colder inside than outside. They find the goods, but not any "extra items" - meanwhile outside Adelei finds a single set of footprints leading into the woods. The team decides to follow. At an old trapper's camp they find as they follow the tracks, the investigators are ambushed by four Frostbitten Wolves, which seem to rise out of the snow. They attach Dan and Adelei, both of whom are knocked prone and Adelei is injured as well. However, the team manage to defeat them and Adelei patches himself up. Grady's Last Stand The trail leads to a clearing in the woods where the frozen corpse of Grady stands with a shotgun in his hands. Around him, his journal and a crate lie half-buried in the snow. The journal nearby documents Grady’s belief that something is stalking the region - “The Wind-Walker ,” a local myth tied to strange totems he had recently intercepted from a rival smuggling group. As Peter tries to grab the shotgun from Grady's hands, his body rises up into the air and comes alive, with ice claws forming on his hands, and a blizzard forming around them. The Frostbound Berserker attacks, flinging ice at the investigators and letting off a horrific shriek. The team manage to take him down with some fine shooting, a machete chop and a blinding light. The blizzard dies down. The crate contains another black totem, with a note from Grady reading "Burn it or he will find you." With the goods obtained, the investigators load up the van and head back to Arkham...

docs.text: The Gate to Hyperborea Arrival in Greenland The investigators had booked a berth in a trading vessel heading to Greenland. They help out on the boat and do some fishing. Adelei manages to cook one of the best meals the crew has ever tasted. Arriving in the key silver mining town of Ivittuut, the team heads to the local inn to find somewhere to stay for the night, and hopefully find out what to do next. The innkeeper tells them that an expedition team arrived a week or so before, and headed off towards some old ruins after getting some directions from the locals. They seemed to be well-equipped and brought all their own sleds etc. with them, rather than hiring locally. However the locals have said that over the last couple of days, they have seen frozen bodies moving about in the distance, and they are worried. Adelei manages to cook another decent meal, so the innkeeper lets him help out that evening. The innkeeper calls over Erik Aunartoq , a local guide who offers to help equip the team and guide them to the ruins. Their sleep is disturbed by shouts and shots from outside - rushing out, they see a group of frozen bodies attacking the locals, who are firing pistols at them (including Erik). Dan Pacho rushes up with his machete to protect Erik, and the others fire their weapons, and they finish the zombies off. Searching the bodies, they find a symbol that they previously found on the cultists in Amos's study - as well as a fragment of a mysterious Hyperborean map. The Glacier Trail Heading off on a pair of sleds pulled by huskies, after several hours they see a crashed sled off to one side. It looks like some of the cultists in the previous expedition crashed and were abandoned, with some trying to head back to town and becoming frozen zombies. McG picks up some spare boots and gloves. Adelei gets the feeling that something is watching the group. Speeding along, Erik spots a crack forming and steers away to avoid it. Peter steers the other sled away as well, as they hear ice cracking below them and an Ice-Wraith emerging. They fire guns at it, but do only slight damage. Adelei casts Azure Flame on it, which does a lot more damage - although he repeatedly sets himself on fire as well. Once the wraith is defeated and disappears into nothingness, the team press on through the storm towards the ruins. The Hidden Ruins After a couple of days travel with no more incident, they arrive at the site of the ruins. McG and Amos are very excited by the Hyperborean runes on some of the pillars, and deduce that they hold instructions to activate a gate in an ancient archway at the centre of the ruins. Adelei tries to gain a vision of Hyperborea, but this time sees a vision of the other side of the gate, looking back at himself on the Greenland side. At this moment, a group of people approach - the lead man introduces himself as Dr. Elias Coldbrook and demands that they hand over the onyx idol to him immediately. He claims that Ithaqua's escape is inevitable, but that if they hand over the idol he would be able to control the Wind-Walker. When the team refuse, he grows angry and instructs his men to take the idol by force. Amos and McG take cover behind some pillars, and McG shoots his Tommy gun towards the cultists. Peter blasts one of the goons with his shotgun, and Peter attacks with his machete, temporarily blinding Elias. Elias tries to cast Storm of Spirits, but with his vision impaired he fails and moments later is severely injured. With the other cultists soon despatched, Elias curses the team and laments that the Earth will be destroyed. McG finds the other half of the map and a journal of Erik's research on Hyperborea and the onyx idol, among other things. The team decide to open the gate to Hyperborea and travel through - leaving Erik behind to look after the huskies. He says that if they are not back in four days, he will have to head back to Ivittuut without them. Adelei casts a spell to open the portal in the archway, and an Ice Colossus rushes out - however it is met with a barrage of bullets, a shotgun blast and finally a machete to its weak spot which shatters it. McG says "Welcome to Earth!" The investigators step through the gate and are surprised at what they find on the other side.

docs.text: The investigators had booked a berth in a trading vessel heading to Greenland. They help out on the boat and do some fishing. Adelei manages to cook one of the best meals the crew has ever tasted. Arriving in the key silver mining town of Ivittuut, the team heads to the local inn to find somewhere to stay for the night, and hopefully find out what to do next. The innkeeper tells them that an expedition team arrived a week or so before, and headed off towards some old ruins after getting some directions from the locals. They seemed to be well-equipped and brought all their own sleds etc. with them, rather than hiring locally. However the locals have said that over the last couple of days, they have seen frozen bodies moving about in the distance, and they are worried. Adelei manages to cook another decent meal, so the innkeeper lets him help out that evening. The innkeeper calls over Erik Aunartoq , a local guide who offers to help equip the team and guide them to the ruins. Their sleep is disturbed by shouts and shots from outside - rushing out, they see a group of frozen bodies attacking the locals, who are firing pistols at them (including Erik). Dan Pacho rushes up with his machete to protect Erik, and the others fire their weapons, and they finish the zombies off. Searching the bodies, they find a symbol that they previously found on the cultists in Amos's study - as well as a fragment of a mysterious Hyperborean map.
docs.title: Arrival in Greenland

docs.text: Heading off on a pair of sleds pulled by huskies, after several hours they see a crashed sled off to one side. It looks like some of the cultists in the previous expedition crashed and were abandoned, with some trying to head back to town and becoming frozen zombies. McG picks up some spare boots and gloves. Adelei gets the feeling that something is watching the group. Speeding along, Erik spots a crack forming and steers away to avoid it. Peter steers the other sled away as well, as they hear ice cracking below them and an Ice-Wraith emerging. They fire guns at it, but do only slight damage. Adelei casts Azure Flame on it, which does a lot more damage - although he repeatedly sets himself on fire as well. Once the wraith is defeated and disappears into nothingness, the team press on through the storm towards the ruins.
docs.title: The Glacier Trail

docs.text: After a couple of days travel with no more incident, they arrive at the site of the ruins. McG and Amos are very excited by the Hyperborean runes on some of the pillars, and deduce that they hold instructions to activate a gate in an ancient archway at the centre of the ruins. Peter blasts one of the goons with his shotgun, and Peter attacks with his machete, temporarily blinding Elias. Elias tries to cast Storm of Spirits, but with his vision impaired he fails and moments later is severely injured. With the other cultists soon despatched, Elias curses the team and laments that the Earth will be destroyed. docs.text: The Icebound Trail Blood in the Streets Arriving back at the back entrance of the Clover Club, the investigators bring in the bootleg alcohol and the idols that they have collected. Seamus is angry about the death of Grady, but is intrigued by the idols. He tells the team that Grady had heard that the Sheldons had done something to disrupt the O'Bannion supply lines, and had captured something that would give some extra information. At this moment, the team hear a shot from outdoors and three thugs burst through the door. The leader takes cover behind a table and fires his Tommy Gun at Adelei, who goes down injured. His two associates take cover and start firing their pistols, but the team manage to take them down - with Dan beheading the leader with his machete. Searching the bodies, they find some strange silver coins and a silk bulletproof vest. McG takes the Tommy Gun from the body of the leader, who turns out to be Clarence Sheldon . The bodies look like they have not eaten for a few days, and their fingers are purple. Seamus is shocked that the Sheldons would start a full-on gang war, and wants the team to find out what is going on - and prevent more bloodshed if possible. McG also has a contact that he can go to to find out more about the silver coins, which have some strange markings and look very old. Hibb's Roadhouse After phoning to arrange a meeting with the Sheldons, the team drive up to Hibb's Roadhouse, which is a couple of miles outside the city. With a couple of heavies outside preventing entry until the team give up their weapons, McG decides to stay in the car to keep watch. Dan tries to smuggle a pistol in, but it is found. Inside, the team meet with Sadie Sheldon , the matriarch of the gang. She tells them that Clarence came to her a couple of weeks ago very pleased with himself. He said he had a way to disrupt the O'Bannions and give the Sheldons an edge - but after that he started acting strangely and they lost contact. She offers a reward for the return of the gun, and also says that she does not want a full-on gang war, and is willing to make a deal with the O'Bannions to find out who did this to her nephew. Adelei convinces her that they don't have the gun, but Peter lets slip that they do have it. Sadie snaps her fingers and her heavies move to block the three investigators inside, while the two outside approach McG and ask him to bring the gun in. He does, and Sadie gives them a reward of $200. The team use the money to pay for another Tommy Gun from the O'Bannions. The Idol's Curse Heading to McG has a contact at Miskatonic University who specialises in old and esoteric artifacts - Professor Amos Derwin . Heading to the Amos's house, they find the him in a panic and the house barricaded shut. McG and Peter manage to convince him to let them in, and Amos relates his tale. He had been approached a couple of weeks ago by some thugs who wanted to know all about The Wind-Walker, and how they might use idols in a ritual. He also notes that the coins are related to the mythical land of Hyperborea, where the Wind-Walker / Ithaqua is imprisoned after rebelling against the other Ancient Ones. At this point, there is a scream from outside, and something tries to smash through the front door. Failing to gain entrance there, there is a crash from other windows until another Frozen Berserker bursts through the kitchen window. It attacks the investigators, and Amos hides under the sofa. Once the berserker is defeated, Amos is worried that something is trying to wipe out any witnesses, and gives a book of spells to Adelei. Adelei uses it to gain a vision of Hyperborea - he sees the giant figure of Ithaqua imprisoned and chained, but at that moment the giant figure pulls at the chain and frees his left hand. Amos also recognises the map that Grady had, and suggests that it shows the location of the ritual site used to activate the idols. It's about four hours drive north, plus a trek into the wilderness. Ambush on the Trail Selling the silver coins to Miskatonic University and using the cash to buy tents and survival equipment, the team head north. After four hours, they park the car and set off on foot. When the sun sets, the team set up camp. Taking it in turns to take watch, McG is on guard when a trio of Wendigos approach the camp. He wakes the others, and retreats to near the fire to gain some protection. Adelei and Peter rush out, while Dan takes is time and eventually comes out in his underwear. The Wendigos rush in and knock over Adelei and McG. The Wendigos are hurt by the investigators, but seem to recover health quickly - but not quickly enough. Once two of them are defeated, Adelei throws a burning branch at the remaining one which seems to stop the health recovery. Eventually all three are killed, and the team take some time to recover and heal their injuries. The next morning, they press on towards the ritual site.

docs.text: The Lost City Through the Gate Stepping through the gate, the investigators find themselves inside a crumbling stone temple. The air is freezing cold, but they feel warmth emanating from the stonework at their feet, which also glows with a strange blue light. Strange plants also grow from cracks in the stonework, and they can see through the archway leading outside that the evening sky is lit with the Aurora Borealis. Amos mentioned that Hyperborea is known as the land of eternal twilight. McG and Amos investigate the carvings on the wall, and they deduce that Hyperborea was founded because of the imprisonment of Ithaqua by the Ancient Ones, and was populated by the servants of the Ancient Ones who did their bidding. This room was obviously a gateway between Hyperborea and Earth and was at one point a commonly used way-station. As they are exploring, they make enough noise that two living statues come to interrupt. They mindlessly attack whoever is nearest - but Dan Pacho guards everyone while they try to work out what to do. Bullets and Shotguns seem to do little damage, but Dan's brass knuckles do the job along with McG smashing them with broken pieces of stone and Peter using his baseball bat. Adelei examines their broken pieces and works out that they were once ordinary statues that have been corrupted and forced to serve Ithaqua's will. Stepping out into the city, the investigators see that they are on the edge of a large bowl, with ruined temples all around the bowl in front of them - and the largest at the bottom of the bowl but reaching up high into the sky. The Fall of Hyperborea The map that McG has pieced together shows the location of the Hall of Records - the team head that way, though the streets are confusing and the investigators have to scramble over and around various objects along the way, with several taking some injuries along the way. At the hall of records, Adelei find reference to The Shard of the Storm which seems to be the lock that was used to imprison Ithaqua. The shard is kept under the temple at the centre of the city, with Ithaqua's prison chamber above it. McG and Amos find more information about how and why Hyperborea fell - in their hubris, the residents of Hyperborea tried to leech Ithaqua's power to empower the city. It backfired when the inhabitants became corrupted and mutated into creatures that served Ithaqua's will. They find notes detailing how the last of Hyperborea's inhabitants fled through the gate to Greenland whilst being pursued by the creatures, which McG recognised. These mutated creatures are like the Messenger that they encountered in the cave near the ritual site. At this moment, Dan raises the alarm as a Messenger creeps up to attack him. Peter is not so lucky and is taken by surprise (though Dan's shout warns him a little). Dan shows his keen machete skills as he brutally dismembers one of the beasts, while the other investigators all focus on the other, eventually managing to kill it. They then head towards the temple at the centre of the city. The Shard of the Storm At the temple of forgotten gods, the investigators head down to try to find the shard of the storm. They hear chanting coming from an underground chamber, and they see a group of cultists performing a ritual around a large onyx stone with lightning bolts constantly flashing inside it. Dan tries to sneak up, but makes a noise at the last moment giving himself away and the the cult leader dodges his machete blow. However this only earns him brief respite as he is shot by Pete and McG, and burnt by Adelei's azure flame. Blinded, he casts storm of spirits - which damages everyone, but he is then swiftly dispatched with the other cultists killed soon after. While McG and Amos discuss whether to use the Shard of the Storm to rebind Ithaqua, or to destroy it to prevent him from using it to travel to Earth, Adelei decides to try to use the stone's power to gain control of storms. He succeeds, but at a terrible cost - he has lost his humanity and sanity in one fell blow. Cackling madly and with a swirling storm surrounding him, Adelei flies out of the temple, and the investigators run outside in time to see him fly into the portal chamber and head back to earth. Heading back that way themselves, they meet up with Erik on the other side and he says he saw something emerge from the gate and fly off. He seems disconcerted, but leads the team back to Ivittuut, where they eventually find a ship to take them back to North America and transport back to Arkham. When they get back to the city, not all is as it was when they left.

docs.text: The Storm Breaks The Frost's Reach Heading back to Arkham, the investigators notice that their fingers are turning purple as they handle the strange silver coins. Adelei has a vision of cultists placing silver coins on the foreheads of people tied down on a large altar. They decide to head to Miskatonic University to consult Amos Derwin. He is in his office and is nervous about opening the door, but upon seeing McG he lets the team in. They start to discuss the coins, and Amos is intrigued by the news that they bring, but at that moment they hear a crash from Amos's storage room next door. Entering the room, they find four cultists, who appear to have raided the room specifically for the silver coins. Three of them seem to have a coin somehow stuck to their forehead, and the last one appears to stick a coin to his forehead as they enter. Two of the cultists then cast a spell that causes injury and panic especially for McG, and the team open fire with all their weapons. Amos is distressed by the damage to his specimens, but is also incensed by people stealing his artifacts so he also joins in with the shooting. Eventually all the cultists die - and Amos then has a panic attack about the four dead bodies now in his rooms. Adelei cuts the coins from the foreheads of the cultists, and McG calls Seamus to try to arrange a cleanup crew. As he relates the tale of what has happened in the office, he hears sudden crashes and bangs from the Clover Club and Seamus shouts "We're under attack!" before the line goes dead. Trouble at the Clover Club The investigators decide to head straight to the Clover Club to help. As they burst in, they see Seamus with two goons firing at a group of six wendigos from a temporary barricade. Adelei rushes in to cast Blinding Light, which affects four of the wendigos, and then the rest of the team fire at will. After taking one of the wendigos down, another cast of Blinding Light affects everyone. Amos is affected so much that he cannot assist for a while. Once all of the wendigos are down, Seamus expresses amazement that the team managed to take them out - as the wendigos has continued to heal up until that point. Peter noticed that the onyx idol glimmered slightly every time a wendigo was injured. Seamus then seems very interested in this idol...

docs.text: The Wrath of the Stormbringer Return to Arkham The city is still experiencing fierce storms. Questioning the locals, the team finds out that a mysterious figure wreathed in storm and shadow has been gathering Ithaqua's followers. They tell Seamus O'Bannion about Adelei, and he suggest meeting with Keith David at the diner, who was Adelei's assistant and protégé. Discussing what they think Adelei's plans may be, they are suddenly fired upon by four cultists. The investigators kill three of them, and knock the last of them to the ground. They try to intimidate him and get information out of him - he mostly babbles incoherently about the coming of the great one, but they do discern the location where Adelei is performing the final ritual to finally free Ithaqua and turn himself into an avatar of the Wind-Walker (Mount Graylock) and find out that the ritual is happening soon. Between them, they also think that there may be a way to sever Adelei's connection to the shard of the storm by disrupting the ritual - though not what the fallout from that may be. The Climb to Mount Graylock Driving to Mount Graylock, the investigators find the mountain covered with a storm and are disturbed by Adelei's voice whispering taunts to them as they start the climb. The going is very tough, and the conditions take their toll with Amos getting injured and all the team suffering the horror of Adelei's words. Halfway up the mountain they encounter a pack of wendigos, which prove tough but fall with the help of Keith casting Azure Flame at each of them. The Ritual of Storm and Blood At the top of the mountain, they find Adelei standing upon a frozen altar, wreathed in crackling energy. Their body is half-human, half-storm and their eyes glow with inhuman fury. Snow and wind swirl unnaturally around them, and the fabric of reality itself seems thinner here. With the ritual started, McG and Keith do their best to disrupt it while Peter and Dan attack Adelei to try to distract them. Adelei pushes on with the ritual and starts casting spells to attack the investigators, and manages to turn incorporeal to frustrate the efforts of Peter and Dan. Keith, Mcg and Amos do manage to do enough to start to disrupt the ritual. Adelei becomes solid again and fights back, but at that moment Adelei's second attempt to turn incorporeal goes wrong and Peter and Dan take this opportunity to inflict multiple injuries on him. Finally Dan rushes up in slow motion and decapitates Adelei, much to Keith's horror. As Adelei's body explodes in a magical burst, the investigators have a vision of an angry Ithaqua trying to escape - but at that moment a rumbling voice overwhelms them and they hear "That is not dead which can eternal lie, And with strange aeons even death may die." and they see Ithaqua's bindings reappear around its limbs. With the storm abating and the sun appearing for the first time in quite a while, the team head back to Arkham to see what the fallout will be - and try not to think about what they may have woken...

Adelei pushes on with the ritual and starts casting spells to attack the investigators, and manages to turn incorporeal to frustrate the efforts of Peter and Dan. Keith, Mcg and Amos do manage to do enough to start to disrupt the ritual. Adelei becomes solid again and fights back, but at that moment Adelei's second attempt to turn incorporeal goes wrong and Peter and Dan take this opportunity to inflict multiple injuries on him. Finally Dan rushes up in slow motion and decapitates Adelei, much to Keith's horror. As Adelei's body explodes in a magical burst, the investigators have a vision of an angry Ithaqua trying to escape - but at that moment a rumbling voice overwhelms them and they hear "That is not dead which can eternal lie, And with strange aeons even death may die." and they see Ithaqua's bindings reappear around its limbs. With the storm abating and the sun appearing for the first time in quite a while, the team head back to Arkham to see what the fallout will be - and try not to think about what they may have woken...
